title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ
titleEn: Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued: Shams al-Dīn Learns the Truth; ʿAjīb and the Cook of Damascus
part: Night 23 · The Tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 176–188 (Night 23, continuing directly from nights-22), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 23 begins with the hunchback groom's flight from the privy and the vizier Shams al-Dīn's discovery, in the turban and the sewn amulet, that the bridegroom of his daughter's wedding night was his own nephew Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan. He records the whole house in writing, and his daughter bears a son, ʿAjīb, who is taunted at school for having no known father. The vizier takes the boy and sets out for Egypt; at Damascus ʿAjīb wanders into the market and meets, without either knowing it, the cook who is his father, and later strikes him with a stone. Verse is copied as printed, and pointed by us only where the print has no marks. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالْعِشْرُونَ قَٰلَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ السَّائِسَ الْأَحْدَبَ صَارَ يُحَدِّثُ الْوَزِيرَ وَالِدَ الْعَرُوسَةِ وَيَقُولُ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ مَنْ كَانَ السَّبَبَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-ʿishrūna qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-sāʾisa al-aḥdaba ṣāra yuḥaddithu al-wazīra wālida al-ʿarūsati wa-yaqūlu laʿana Allāhu man kāna al-sababa
sentences.l: And-when was the-night the-third and-the-twenty, she-said: It-has-reached-me, O king the-fortunate, that the-groom the-hunchback came-to-be conversing-with the-vizier, father-of the-bride, and-saying: God-has-cursed whoever was the-cause.
sentences.i: And when it was the twenty-third night, she said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the hunchbacked groom began talking with the vizier, the bride's father, and saying: God curse whoever was the cause of it!
sentences.n: قلت is printed for قالت; it is read qālat, "she said" (Shahrazād). The night's number is printed والعشرون in the nominative where Classical would have the genitive after the feminine ordinal; I point what is printed. السائس is the groom of horses, here the hunchback who was foisted on the bride; the vizier is her father. لعن الله من كان السبب is the groom's curse, "may God curse whoever was the cause".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْوَزِيرُ قُمْ وَاخْرُجْ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-wazīru qum wa-ukhruj min hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-vizier: Rise and-go-out from this the-place.
sentences.i: Then the vizier said to him, "Get up and go out of this place."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ أَنَا مَجْنُونٌ أَرُوحُ مَعَكَ بِغَيْرِ إِذْنِ الْعِفْرِيتِ فَإِنَّهُ قَٰلَ لِي إِذَا طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ اخْرُجْ وَرُحْ إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ فَطَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُ أَمْ لَا فَإِنِّي لَا أَقْدِرُ أَطْلَعُ مِنْ مَوْضِعِي إِلَّا أَنْ طَلَعَتِ الشَّمْسُنْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu anā majnūnun arūḥu maʿaka bi-ghayri idhni al-ʿifrīti fa-innahu qāla lī idhā ṭalaʿati al-shamsu ukhruj wa-ruḥ ilā ḥāli sabīlika fa-ṭalaʿati al-shamsu am lā fa-innī lā aqdiru aṭlaʿu min mawḍiʿī illā an ṭalaʿati al-shamsun
sentences.l: And-said to-him: I (am) mad! I-go with-you without permission-of the-ifrit? For-indeed-he said to-me: When has-risen the-sun, go-out and-go to the-state-of your-way. And-has-the-sun-risen or not? For-indeed-I not I-am-able (that) I-come-out from my-place, except that has-risen the-sun.
sentences.i: And he said to him, "Am I mad, to go with you without the ifrit's permission? He told me: When the sun has risen, come out and go your way. Has the sun risen, or not? For I cannot come out from my place unless the sun has risen."
sentences.n: قل is printed for قال (dagger alif: qāla); this slip recurs in this night. أَرُوحُ مَعَكَ and أَقْدِرُ أَطْلَعُ are colloquial: a bare imperfect where Classical would have an introducing particle or أَنْ ("I am able to come out"). إِلَى حَالِ سَبِيلِكَ, "to the state of your way", is the idiom "go about your business". At the end the print has الشمسن, with a stray ن after the word; it is read al-shams, and the ن is pointed as a silent letter. The same slip appears again below.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَالَ الْوَزِيرُ مَنْ أَتَى بِكَ إِلَى هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāla al-wazīru man atā bika ilā hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: And-at that said the-vizier: Who brought you to this the-place?
sentences.i: At that the vizier said, "Who brought you to this place?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنِّي جِئْتُ الْبَارِحَةَ إِلَى هُنَا لِأَقْضِيَ حَاجَتِى وَأُزِيلَ ضَرُورَتِي وَإِذَا بِفَارَةٍ طَلَعَ مِنْ وَسَطِ الْمَاءِ وَعَيَّطَ وَصَارَ يَكْبُرُ حَتَّى بَقِيَ قَدْرَ الْجَامُوسَةِ وَ قَالَ لِي كَلَامٌ دَخَلَ فِي أُذْنِى فَخَلَّانِي وَرَاحَ لَعَنَ اللَّهُ الْعَرُوسَةَ وَمَنْ زَوَّجَنِي بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla innī jiʾtu al-bāriḥata ilā hunā li-aqḍiya ḥājatī wa-uzīla ḍarūratī wa-idhā bi-fāratin ṭalaʿa min wasaṭi al-māʾi wa-ʿayyaṭa wa-ṣāra yakburu ḥattā baqiya qadra al-jāmūsati wa qāla lī kalāmun dakhala fī udhnī fa-khallānī wa-rāḥa laʿana Allāhu al-ʿarūsata wa-man zawwajanī bihā
sentences.l: And-he-said: Indeed-I I-came last-night to here to-I-fulfil my-need and-remove my-necessity, and-behold with-a-mouse (that) came-up from the-middle-of the-water, and-cried-out, and-came-to-be growing-large until it-was the-measure-of the-buffalo; and it-said to-me words (that) entered into my-ear; and-it-left-me and-went. God-has-cursed the-bride and-whoever married-me to-her!
sentences.i: He said, "I came here last night to relieve myself and ease my need, and behold, a mouse came up out of the middle of the water and shrieked, and it kept growing until it was the size of a buffalo. And it spoke some words to me that entered my ear, and then it left me and went. God curse the bride, and whoever married me to her!"
sentences.n: Several colloquial touches. فَارَة (for فَأْرَة) is Egyptian for "mouse", the jinni's disguise. The print splits و from قال at the line end (و قال), and the pointing keeps the split. وعيط is colloquial (ʿayyaṭa) for "cried out". كَلَامٌ دَخَلَ فِي أُذْنِى has no connecting word before the verb, where Classical would say "words which entered"; I point كَلَامٌ as printed, a bare noun, not كَلَامًا. حاجتى and اذنى are printed with ى for ي. لِأَقْضِيَ حَاجَتِى and أُزِيلَ ضَرُورَتِي is the polite way of saying he had gone to the privy.

sentences.t: فَتَقَدَّمَ إِلَيْهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَأَخْرَجَهُ مِنَ الْمِرْحَاضِ فَخَرَجَ وَهُوَ يَجْرِي وَمَا صَدَّقَ أَنَّ الشَّمْسُنْ طَلَعَتْ وَطَلَعَ إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِمَا اتَّفَقَ لَهُ مَعَ الْعِفْرِيتِ
sentences.tr: fa-taqaddama ilayhi al-wazīru wa-akhrajahu mina al-mirḥāḍi fa-kharaja wa-huwa yajrī wa-mā ṣaddaqa anna al-shamsun ṭalaʿat wa-ṭalaʿa ilā al-sulṭāni wa-aʿlamahu bi-mā ittafaqa lahu maʿa al-ʿifrīti
sentences.l: And-advanced to-him the-vizier and-brought-him-out from the-privy; and-he-went-out and-he running, and-not he-believed that the-sun had-risen; and-he-went-up to the-sultan and-informed-him with-what befell to-him with the-ifrit.
sentences.i: The vizier came forward and brought him out of the privy, and he ran off, hardly believing that the sun had risen; and he went up to the sultan and told him what had befallen him with the ifrit.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْوَزِيرُ أَبُو الْعَرُوسَةِ فَإِنَّهُ دَخَلَ الْبَيْتَ وَهُوَ حَائِرُ الْعَقْلِ فِي أَمْرِ ابْنَتِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-wazīru abū al-ʿarūsati fa-innahu dakhala al-bayta wa-huwa ḥāʾiru al-ʿaqli fī amri ibnatihi
sentences.l: And-as-for the-vizier, father-of the-bride, then-indeed-he entered the-house, and-he bewildered-of the-mind concerning the-affair-of his-daughter.
sentences.i: As for the vizier, the bride's father, he went into the house bewildered in his mind over the matter of his daughter.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا بِنْتِي اكْشِفِي لِي خَبَرَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā bintī ikshifī lī khabaraki
sentences.l: And-he-said: O my-daughter, uncover for-me your-news.
sentences.i: He said, "My daughter, tell me plainly what has happened to you."
sentences.n: بِنْت for ابْنَة, "daughter", is the colloquial form and is pointed as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ إِنَّ الْعَرِيسَ الَّذِي كُنْتُ أَنْجَلِي عَلَيْهِ الْبَارِحَةَ بَاتَ عِنْدِي وَأَخَذَ وَجْهِي وَعَلِقْتُ مِنْهُ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَمْ تُصَدِّقْنِي هَذَا شَاشُهُ بِلَفْتِهِ عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ وَلِبَاسُهُ تَحْتَ الْفَرْشِ وَفِيهِ شَيْءٌ مَلْفُوفٌ وَلَمْ أَعْرِفْ مَاهُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat inna al-ʿarīsa alladhī kuntu anjalī ʿalayhi al-bāriḥata bāta ʿindī wa-akhadha wajhī wa-ʿaliqtu minhu wa-in kunta lam tuṣaddiqnī hādhā shāshuhu bi-laftihi ʿalā al-kursiyyi wa-libāsuhu taḥta al-farshi wa-fīhi shayʾun malfūfun wa-lam aʿrif māhuwa
sentences.l: And-she-said: Indeed the-bridegroom who I-was I-am-displayed to-him last-night spent-the-night with-me and-took my-face, and-I-conceived by-him. And-if you-were not you-believe-me: this his-turban-cloth, in-its-winding, on the-chair, and-his-drawers under the-bedding, and-in-them a-thing wrapped, and-not I-knew what-it.
sentences.i: She said, "The bridegroom to whom I was displayed last night spent the night with me, and took my maidenhead, and I have conceived by him. And if you do not believe me, here is his turban-cloth, still wound as he left it, on the chair, and his drawers are under the bedding, with something wrapped up in them, and I did not know what it was."
sentences.n: أَخَذَ وَجْهِي, "he took my face", is a euphemism for taking her virginity (the Arabic also uses "face" for honour); she goes on to say she has conceived. كُنْتُ أَنْجَلِي is "I was being displayed" (jilwa, the unveiling of the bride). كنت أنجلي, كان with a bare imperfect, is the ordinary continuous past. شَاشُهُ بِلَفْتِهِ reads "his turban-cloth with its winding", that is, still wound as it was; the print gives no vowels, and لَفْتَهُ ("a wind of it") is the alternative. ماهو is run together; read مَا هُوَ.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ وَالِدُهَا هَذَا الْكَلَامَ دَخَلَ الْبَشْخَانَهْ فَوَجَدَ شَاشَ بَدْرِ الدِّينِ حَسَنِ بْنِ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa wāliduhā hādhā al-kalāma dakhala al-bashkhānah fa-wajada shāsha badri al-dīni ḥasani ibni akhīhi
sentences.l: And-when heard her-father this the-speech, he-entered the-bashkhana, and-found the-turban-cloth-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan son-of his-brother.
sentences.i: When her father heard this, he went into the bashkhana and found the turban-cloth of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, his brother's son.
sentences.n: البشخانه (bashkhāna) is a Persian-derived word for a chamber in the house; the exact room is uncertain to me. The print has ه for the usual ة, and I point it as a pausal -ah. شاش is the turban's muslin.

sentences.t: فَفِي الْحَالِ أَخَذَهُ فِي يَدِهِ وَقَلَّبَهُ وَقَٰلَ هَذِهِ عِمَامَةٌ وُزَرَٰأَ لِأَنَّهَا مَوْصِلِيَّةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-fī al-ḥāli akhadhahu fī yadihi wa-qallabahu wa-qāla hādhihi ʿimāmatun wuzarāʾa li-annahā mawṣiliyyatun
sentences.l: And-in the-moment he-took-it in his-hand and-turned-it-over, and-said: This a-turban, viziers; because-it Mosuli.
sentences.i: At once he took it in his hand and turned it over, and said, "This is a vizier's turban, for it is of Mosul make."
sentences.n: وزرأ is printed for وُزَرَاء (wuzarāʾ), "viziers"; the long ā is marked with a dagger alif and the hamza kept as printed. The two words عمامة وزرأ are printed apart, and I point عِمَامَةٌ as an indefinite noun followed by the plural, "a turban, viziers'", that is, a vizier's turban. موصلية is a muslin from Mosul, a costly stuff. قل for قال again.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ إِلَى حِرْزٍ مَخِيطٍ فِي طَرْبُوشِهِ فَأَخَذَهُ وَفَتَقَهُ وَأَخَذَ اللِّبَاسَ فَوَجَدَ الْكِيسَ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ فَفَتَحَهُ فَوَجَدَ فِيهِ وَرَقَةً فَقَرَأَهَا فَوَجَدَ مُبَايَعَةَ الْيَهُودِيِّ وَاسْمَ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنِ بْنِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ الْمِصْرِيِّ وَوَجَدَ الْأَلْفَ دِينَارٍ
sentences.tr: thumma naẓara ilā ḥirzin makhīṭin fī ṭarbūshihi fa-akhadhahu wa-fataqahu wa-akhadha al-libāsa fa-wajada al-kīsa alladhī fīhi al-alfu dīnārin fa-fataḥahu fa-wajada fīhi waraqatan fa-qaraʾahā fa-wajada mubāyaʿata al-yahūdiyyi wa-isma badri al-dīni ḥasani ibni nūri al-dīni ʿaliyyin al-miṣriyyi wa-wajada al-alfa dīnārin
sentences.l: Then he-looked at an-amulet sewn in his-tarbush, and-took-it and-ripped-it-open, and-took the-drawers, and-found the-purse which in-it the-thousand dinar; and-opened-it and-found in-it a-paper, and-read-it, and-found the-sale-contract-of the-Jew and-the-name-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan son-of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī the-Egyptian; and-found the-thousand dinar.
sentences.i: Then he noticed a charm sewn into the tarbush, and took it and ripped it open. He took up the drawers and found the purse with the thousand dinars in it; he opened it and found a paper inside, and read it, and found the Jew's bill of sale, and the name of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan son of Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī the Egyptian; and he found the thousand dinars.
sentences.n: حِرْز is an amulet or charm, here a folded paper sewn into the cap. الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ is "the thousand of dinars", with the article on the first term only. The edition prints قرأ (qaraʾa) with a precomposed hamza and I keep it. بدرالدين and نورالدين are printed run together.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرَأَ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ الْوَرَقَةَ صَرَخَ صَرْخَةً وَخَرَّ مَغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qaraʾa shamsu al-dīni al-waraqata ṣarakha ṣarkhatan wa-kharra maghshiyyan ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-when read Shams al-Dīn the-paper, he-cried-out a-cry and-fell overcome upon-him.
sentences.i: When Shams al-Dīn read the paper, he cried out a great cry and fell down in a swoon.
sentences.n: ṣarakha ṣarkhatan, "he cried a cry", is an intensifying cognate accusative. مغشيا عليه, "covered over", is the stock expression for fainting.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَ وَعَلِمَ مَضْمُونَ الْقِصَّةِ تَعَجَّبَ وَقَالَ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْقَادِرُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيٍّ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqa wa-ʿalima maḍmūna al-qiṣṣati taʿajjaba wa-qāla lā ilāha illā Allāhu al-qādiru ʿalā kulli shayyin
sentences.l: And-when he-recovered and-knew the-contents-of the-story, he-marvelled and-said: No god but God, the-Able over every thing.
sentences.i: When he came to himself and understood what the story contained, he marvelled and said, "There is no god but God, who has power over all things."
sentences.n: شي is printed for شَيْء (shayʾ), "thing", with the hamza dropped, as often; I point it shayy.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا بِنْتِي تَعْرِفِينَ مَنِ الَّذِي أَخَذَ وَجْهَكِ قَالَتْ لَا قَالَ إِنَّهُ ابْنُ أَخِي وَهُوَ ابْنُ عَمِّكِ وَهَذِهِ الْأَلْفُ دِينَارٍ مَهْرُكِ فَسُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ فَلَيْتَ شِعْرِي كَيْفَ اتَّفَقَتْ هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā bintī taʿrifīna mani alladhī akhadha wajhaki qālat lā qāla innahu ibnu akhī wa-huwa ibnu ʿammiki wa-hādhihi al-alfu dīnārin mahruki fa-subḥāna Allāhi fa-layta shiʿrī kayfa ittafaqat hādhihi al-qiṣṣatu
sentences.l: And-he-said: O my-daughter, do-you-know who (is) the-one-who took your-face? She-said: No. He-said: Indeed-he (is) son-of my-brother, and-he (is) son-of your-uncle, and-this the-thousand dinar (is) your-dower. So glory-be-to God! And-would-that my-perception (were with me): how came-about this the-story!
sentences.i: And he said, "My daughter, do you know who it was that took your maidenhead?" She said, "No." He said, "He is the son of my brother, and so your cousin, and these thousand dinars are your dower. Glory be to God! Would that I knew how this story came about!"
sentences.n: The father's reply is reported inside the same sentence as the exchange before it, with no mark of change of speaker; قالت لا قال إنه is "she said: No. He said: He is...". فَلَيْتَ شِعْرِي, "would that my knowing (were mine)", is a set phrase for "if only I knew", followed by an indirect question.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ فَتَحَ الْحِرْزَ الْمَخِيطَ فَوَجَدَ فِيهِ وَرَقَةً مَكْتُوبَةً وَمَكْتُوبٌ فِيهَا تَارِيخٌ بِخَطِّ أَخِيهِ نُورِالدِّينِ الْمِصْرِيِّ أَبُو بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ
sentences.tr: thumma fataḥa al-ḥirza al-makhīṭa fa-wajada fīhi waraqatan maktūbatan wa-maktūbun fīhā tārīkhun bi-khaṭṭi akhīhi nūri al-dīni al-miṣriyyi abū badri al-dīni ḥasanin
sentences.l: Then he-opened the-amulet the-sewn, and-found in-it a-paper written, and-written in-it a-date in the-handwriting-of his-brother Nūr al-Dīn the-Egyptian, father-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.i: Then he opened the sewn charm and found in it a written paper, with a date written on it in the hand of his brother Nūr al-Dīn the Egyptian, the father of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.n: أَبُو is in the nominative, though it stands in apposition to a word in the genitive (أَخِيهِ نُورِالدِّينِ), where Classical would have أَبِي. This is the ordinary Middle Arabic habit of leaving the "five nouns" in the nominative; I point what is printed. The date is the day of the boy's conception, which settles his identity.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَخَطَّ أَخِيهِ أَنْشَدَ وَقَالَ هَذِهِ الْأَ بْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara-khaṭṭa akhīhi anshada wa-qāla hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And-when he-looked-at-the-handwriting-of his-brother, he-recited and-said: These the-verses.
sentences.i: When he saw his brother's handwriting, he recited these verses:
sentences.n: Two words are run together in the print (نظرخط for نَظَرَ خَطَّ) and one is split (الا بيات for الْأَبْيَاتَ); the pointing keeps the printed divisions.

sentences.t:
اَرِي آثَارَهُمْ فَاَذُوبُ شَوْقاً * وَاَسْكُبُ فِي مَوَاطِنِهِمْ دُمُوعِي
وَاَسْاَلُ مَنْ بِفُرْقَتِهِمْ رَمَانِي * يَمُنُّ عَلَيَّ يَوْماً بِالرُّجُوعِ
sentences.tr:
arī āthārahum fa-adhūbu shawqan * wa-askubu fī mawāṭinihim dumūʿī
wa-asʾalu man bi-furqatihim ramānī * yamunnu ʿalayya yawman bi-al-rujūʿi
sentences.l:
I-see their-traces, so-I-melt (with) longing, * and-I-pour in their-abodes my-tears;
and-I-ask whoever with-their-parting struck-me * (that) he-favour upon-me (on) a-day with-the-return.
sentences.i: I see their traces and melt with longing, and pour out my tears in the places where they dwelt; and I ask the one whose parting from them has struck me down to grant me, some day, the grace of return.
sentences.n: The verse is printed pointed and is copied exactly as printed. Note the printed kasra in اَرِي (read arā in Classical; here arī, "I see") and the hamza left unwritten in اَذُوبُ, وَاَسْكُبُ and وَاَسْاَلُ. يَمُنُّ عَلَيَّ is a wish in the indicative, "may he grant me"; the verb takes the preposition عَلَى for the person favoured.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ قَرَأَ الْحِرْزَ فَوَجَدَ فِيهِ تَارِيخَ زَوَاجِهِ بِنْتَ وَزِيرِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَتَارِيخَ دُخُولِهِ وَتَارِيخَ مَوْلِدِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ وَتَارِيخَ عُمْرِهِ إِلَى حِينِ وَفَاتِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha mina al-shiʿri qaraʾa al-ḥirza fa-wajada fīhi tārīkha zawājihi binta wazīri al-baṣrati wa-tārīkha dukhūlihi wa-tārīkha mawlidi badri al-dīni ḥasanin wa-tārīkha ʿumrihi ilā ḥīni wafātihi
sentences.l: And-when he-finished from the-poetry, he-read the-amulet and-found in-it the-date-of his-marriage the-daughter-of the-vizier-of Basra, and-the-date-of his-entering, and-the-date-of the-birth-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-the-date-of his-age up-to the-time-of his-death.
sentences.i: When he had finished the poem, he read the charm, and found in it the date of his marriage to the daughter of the vizier of Basra, the date of his going in to her, the date of the birth of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and the date of his age up to the hour of his death.
sentences.n: الحرز is the amulet-case that held the written paper. 'His' marriage and age are the dead brother's, whose record the paper is; the vizier then sets it beside his own life (next sentence).

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ وَاهْتَزَّ مِنَ الطَّرَبِ وَقَابَلَ مَا جَرَٰي لِأَخِيهِ عَلَى مَا جَرَٰي لَهُ فَوَجَدَهُ سَوَاءً بِسَوَاءٍ وَزَوَاجُهُ وَزَوَاجُ الْآخَرِ مُتَوَافِقَيْنِ تَارِيخًا وَالدُّخُولُ وَوِلَادَةُ بَدْرِالدِّينِ وَبِنْتِهِ سِتِّ الْحُسْنِ أَيْضًا مُوَافِقًا
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba wa-ihtazza mina al-ṭarabi wa-qābala mā jarā li-akhīhi ʿalā mā jarā lahu fa-wajadahu sawāʾan bi-sawāʾin wa-zawājuhu wa-zawāju al-ākhari mutawāfiqayni tārīkhan wa-al-dukhūlu wa-wilādatu badri al-dīni wa-bintihi sitti al-ḥusni ayḍan muwāfiqan
sentences.l: And-he-marvelled and-was-shaken from the-delight, and-compared what happened to-his-brother with what happened to-him, and-found-it alike by-alike: his-marriage and-the-marriage-of the-other agreeing in-date, and-the-entering, and-the-birth-of Badr al-Dīn and-of-his-daughter Sitt al-Ḥusn, also agreeing.
sentences.i: He marvelled, and was shaken with delight; and he set what had befallen his brother beside what had befallen himself, and found them exactly alike: his marriage and the other's agreed in date, and so did the going-in, and the birth of Badr al-Dīn and of his daughter Sitt al-Ḥusn.
sentences.n: اهتز من الطرب, 'was stirred with delight'. مُوَافِقًا is singular where the sense is plural, and the endings of متوافقين and موافقا do not follow Classical agreement; both are kept as printed.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ الْوَرَقَةَ وَطَلَعَ بِهَا إِلَى السُّلْطَانِ وَأَعْلَمَهُ بِمَا جَرَٰي مِنْ أَوَّلِ الْأَمْرِ إِلَى آخِرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha al-waraqata wa-ṭalaʿa bihā ilā al-sulṭāni wa-aʿlamahu bi-mā jarā min awwali al-amri ilā ākhirihi
sentences.l: And-he-took the-paper and-went-up with-it to the-sultan, and-informed-him of-what happened from first-of the-affair to its-last.
sentences.i: He took the paper, went up with it to the sultan, and told him all that had happened from the beginning of the affair to its end.
sentences.n: جَرَٰي is printed جري for جرى; the dagger alif marks the reading jarā.

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْمَلِكُ وَأَمَرَأَنْ يُؤَرَّخَ هَذَا الْأَمْرُ فِى الْحَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-maliku wa-amara an yuʾarrakha hādhā al-amru fī al-ḥāli
sentences.l: And-marvelled the-king, and-commanded that be-dated this the-affair in the-moment.
sentences.i: The king marvelled, and ordered that the whole affair be written down, with its dates, at once.
sentences.n: وامران is وأمر أن run together in the print. يُؤَرَّخَ is read as a passive, 'be dated, be entered in the record'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقَامَ الْوَزِيرُ يَنْتَظِرُ ابْنَ أَخِيهِ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمَ فَمَا أَتَى وَثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ وَثَالِثَ يَوْمٍ إِلَى سَبْعَةِ أَيَّامٍ فَمَا وَقَعَ لَهُ عَلَى خَبَرٍ
sentences.tr: thumma aqāma al-wazīru yantaẓiru ibna akhīhi dhālika al-yawma fa-mā atā wa-thāniya yawmin wa-thālitha yawmin ilā sabʿati ayyāmin fa-mā waqaʿa lahu ʿalā khabarin
sentences.l: Then stayed the-vizier waiting-for son-of his-brother that the-day, and-not he-came; and-second-of day and-third-of day, up-to seven-of days, and-not fell for-him upon news.
sentences.i: Then the vizier stayed on, waiting for his brother's son that day, but he did not come; nor the second day, nor the third, up to seven days, and he came upon no news of him.
sentences.n: أقام ينتظر, 'he stayed waiting', is the common 'stay and do' construction. وقع على خبر, 'light upon news'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَأَعْمَلَنَّ عَمَلًا مَا سَبَقَنِي إِلَيْهِ أَحَدٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-Allāhi la-aʿmalanna ʿamalan mā sabaqanī ilayhi aḥadun
sentences.l: And-he-said: By-God, I-will-surely-do a-deed not has-preceded-me to-it anyone.
sentences.i: And he said, "By God, I will do a deed that no one has done before me."

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ دَوَاةً وَقَلَمًا وَكَتَبَ فِي وَرَقَةٍ صُورَةَ نَصْبِ الْبَيْتِ جَمِيعِهِ وَأَنَّ الْخَشْخَانَةَ مَوْضِعُ كَذَا وَالسِّتَارَةَ الْفُلَانِيَّةَ مَوْضِعُ كَذَا وَجَمِيعَ مَا فِى الْبَيْتِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha dawātan wa-qalaman wa-kataba fī waraqatin ṣūrata naṣbi al-bayti jamīʿihi wa-anna al-khashkhānata mawḍiʿu kadhā wa-al-sitārata al-fulāniyyata mawḍiʿu kadhā wa-jamīʿa mā fī al-bayti
sentences.l: And-he-took an-inkwell and-a-pen, and-wrote on a-sheet the-form-of the-setting-up-of the-house, all-of-it, and that the-khashkhana is place-of such-and-such, and-the-curtain the-so-and-so is place-of such-and-such, and all-of what is in the-house.
sentences.i: He took an inkwell and a pen and wrote on a sheet a plan of the whole furnishing of the house: that the khashkhana stood in such a place, and such-and-such a curtain in such a place, and everything else that was in the house.
sentences.n: الخشخانة (khashkhāna) is a chamber or alcove of the house; the exact sense is uncertain. نصب البيت is 'the setting-up' of the house, its fittings and layout. The two كذا are 'such-and-such a place'.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ طَوَى الْكِتَابَ وَأَمَرَ بِشَيْلِ الْحَوَائِجِ وَأَخَذَ الشَّاشَ وَالطَّرْبُوشَ وَأَخَذَ الْفَرَجِيَّةَ وَالْكِيسَ وَشَالَهُمْ عِنْدَهُ وَقَفَلَهُمْ بِقُفْلٍ مِنْ حَدِيدٍ وَخَتَمَ عَلَيْهِ إِلَى أَنْ يَصِلَ ابْنُ أَخِيهِ حَسَنٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ
sentences.tr: thumma ṭawā al-kitāba wa-amara bi-shayli al-ḥawāʾiji wa-akhadha al-shāsha wa-al-ṭarbūsha wa-akhadha al-farajiyyata wa-al-kīsa wa-shālahum ʿindahu wa-qafalahum bi-quflin min ḥadīdin wa-khatama ʿalayhi ilā an yaṣila ibnu akhīhi ḥasanun al-baṣriyyu
sentences.l: Then he-folded the-writing and-commanded the-lifting-away-of the-belongings, and-took the-muslin and-the-tarboosh, and-took the-farajiyya and-the-purse, and-lifted-them-away at-him, and-locked-them with-a-lock of iron and-sealed upon-it, until arrives son-of his-brother Ḥasan the-Basran.
sentences.i: Then he folded the writing and gave orders for the belongings to be lifted away. He took the muslin and the tarboosh, the farajiyya and the purse, and put them away in his own keeping, locked them with an iron lock and sealed it, until his brother's son Ḥasan of Basra should arrive.
sentences.n: شيل (verbal noun of شال) and شالهم are colloquial Egyptian, 'carrying off, putting away'. الشاش is turban-muslin, الطربوش the tarboosh cap, الفرجية a long loose robe, الكيس a purse. وقفلهم and ختم عليه: the lock (and seal) is on the storeroom or chest holding them.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بِنْتُ الْوَزِيرِ فَتَمَّتْ أَشْهُرُهَا وَوَلَدَتْ وَلَدًا مِثْلَ الْقَمَرِ شَبِيهَ وَالِدِهِ فِى الْحُسْنِ وَالْكَمَالِ وَالْبَهَاءِ وَالْجَمَالِ فَقَطَعُوا سُرَّتَهُ وَكَحَّلُوا مُقْلَنَهُ وَسَلَّمُوهُ إِلَى الدَّايَاتِ وَسَمَّوْهُ عَجِيبًا
sentences.tr: wa-ammā bintu al-wazīri fa-tammat ashhuruhā wa-waladat waladan mithla al-qamari shabīha wālidihi fī al-ḥusni wa-al-kamāli wa-al-bahāʾi wa-al-jamāli fa-qaṭaʿū surratahu wa-kaḥḥalū muqlanahu wa-sallamūhu ilā al-dāyāti wa-sammawhu ʿajīban
sentences.l: And-as-for the-daughter-of the-vizier, her-months were-completed and-she-bore a-boy like the-moon, resembling-of his-father in the-beauty and-the-perfection and-the-splendour and-the-comeliness; and-they-cut his-navel-cord and-kohled his-eye and-handed-him to the-nurses and-named-him ʿAjīb.
sentences.i: As for the vizier's daughter, her months were completed and she bore a boy like the moon, the very likeness of his father in beauty, perfection, splendour and grace. They cut his navel-cord, kohled his eyes, gave him over to the nurses, and named him ʿAjīb.
sentences.n: مقلنه is printed for مقلته (ن for ت), 'his eye'; the vocalisation follows the print. الدايات, 'nurses', is the colloquial dāya. عجيب means 'wondrous, strange'.

sentences.t: فَصَارَ يَوْمُهُ بِشَهْرٍ . شَهْرُهُ بِسَنَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra yawmuhu bi-shahrin . shahruhu bi-sanatin
sentences.l: And-became his-day with-a-month; his-month with-a-year.
sentences.i: And his day came to count as a month, and his month as a year.
sentences.n: The full stop falls inside the sentence in the print. The two balanced clauses say that he grew with astonishing speed; بِـ is 'worth, equal to'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ أَعْطَاهُ لِفَقِيهٍ وَوَصَّاهُ أَنْ يُرَبِّيَهُ وَيُقْرِئَهُ وَيُحْسِنَ تَرْبِيَتَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā marra ʿalayhi sabʿu sinīna aʿṭāhu li-faqīhin wa-waṣṣāhu an yurabbiyahu wa-yuqriʾahu wa-yuḥsina tarbiyatahu
sentences.l: And-when passed upon-him seven years, he-gave-him to-a-jurist and-charged-him to-rear-him and-have-him-recite and-do-well his-upbringing.
sentences.i: When seven years had passed over him, he gave him to a schoolmaster and charged him to rear him, to teach him to read, and to take good care of his upbringing.
sentences.n: سبع سنين keeps the oblique -īn after a numeral in the nominative, as in everyday speech. The فقيه is the schoolmaster of the maktab. يقرئه is 'make him read', that is, teach him the Qurʾān and reading.

sentences.t: فَقَامَ فِى الْمَكْتَبِ أَرْبَعَ سَبَوَاتٍ فَصَارَ يُقَاتِلُ أَهْلَ الْمَكْتَبِ وَيَسُبُّهُمْ وَيَقُولُ لَهُمْ مَنْ فِيكُمْ مِثْلِي أَنَا ابْنُ وَزِيرِ مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma fī al-maktabi arbaʿa sabawātin fa-ṣāra yuqātilu ahla al-maktabi wa-yasubbuhum wa-yaqūlu lahum man fīkum mithlī anā ibnu wazīri miṣra
sentences.l: And-he-stayed in the-school four sabawāt [years], and-began fighting the-people-of the-school and-cursing-them and-saying to-them: Who in-you is-like-me? I am son-of vizier-of Egypt.
sentences.i: He stayed at school four years, and took to fighting the other boys and abusing them, saying, "Who among you is like me? I am the son of the vizier of Egypt."
sentences.n: سبوات is printed for سنوات, 'years' (ب for ن); it is vocalised as printed and read sanawāt. قام في المكتب, 'stayed at school'. صار يقاتل, 'began to fight', is the usual 'become + verb' inceptive.

sentences.t: فَقَامَتِ الْأَوْلَادُ وَاجْتَمَعُوا يَشْكُونَ لِلْعَرِيفِ مِمَّا قَاسَوْهُ مِنْ عَجِيبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāmati al-awlādu wa-ijtamaʿū yashkūna li-al-ʿarīfi mimmā qāsawhu min ʿajībin
sentences.l: And-rose the-children and-they-gathered, complaining to-the-monitor of-what they-suffered from ʿAjīb.
sentences.i: Then the boys rose up and gathered, and complained to the monitor of what they suffered from ʿAjīb.
sentences.n: قامت الأولاد: a feminine singular verb before a plural noun, as the print often has it, followed by plural verbs. العريف is the monitor, the senior boy or assistant who looks after the others.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمُ الْعَرِيفُ غَدًا لَمَّايَجِي أُعَلِّمُكُمْ شَيْئًا تَقُولُوهُ لَهُ فَيَتُوبَ عَنِ الْمَجِي لِلْمَكْتَبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahumu al-ʿarīfu ghadan lammā yajī uʿallimukum shayʾan taqūlūhu lahu fa-yatūba ʿani al-majī li-al-maktabi
sentences.l: And-said to-them the-monitor: Tomorrow when he-comes I-will-teach-you a-thing you-say-it to-him, so-that-he-repent from the-coming to-the-school.
sentences.i: The monitor said to them, "Tomorrow, when he comes, I will teach you something to say to him, so that he gives up coming to school."
sentences.n: لمايجي is لَمَّا يَجِي, 'when he comes', written as one word; يجي and المجي are colloquial spellings for يجيء and المجيء. تقولوه drops the final nūn (تقولونه) in a relative clause, a regular Middle Arabic habit.

sentences.t: وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُ إِذَا جَاءَ غَدًا فَاقْعُدُوا حَوْلَهُ وَقُولُوا لِبَعْضِكُمْ بَعْضًا وَاللَّهِ مَا يَلْعَبُ مَعَنَا هَذِهِ اللُّعْبَةَ إِلَّا مَنْ يَقُولُ لَنَا عَلَى اسْمِ أُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ وَمَنْ لَمْ يَعْرِفِ اسْمَ أُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ فَهُوَ ابْنُ حَرَامٍ فَلَمْ يَلْعَبْ مَعَنَا
sentences.tr: wa-dhālika annahu idhā jāʾa ghadan fa-iqʿudū ḥawlahu wa-qūlū li-baʿḍikum baʿḍan wa-Allāhi mā yalʿabu maʿanā hādhihi al-luʿbata illā man yaqūlu lanā ʿalā ismi ummihi wa-abīhi wa-man lam yaʿrifi isma ummihi wa-abīhi fa-huwa ibnu ḥarāmin fa-lam yalʿab maʿanā
sentences.l: And-that is that-he, when he-comes tomorrow, then-sit around-him and-say to-each-of-you the-other: By-God, not plays with-us this the-game except he-who says to-us upon the-name-of his-mother and-his-father; and-he-who not knows the-name-of his-mother and-his-father, he is son-of the-forbidden; so-not he-plays with-us.
sentences.i: "Here is the plan: when he comes tomorrow, sit down around him and say to one another, 'By God, no one plays this game with us unless he can tell us the name of his mother and his father; and whoever does not know the name of his mother and father is a bastard, and shall not play with us.'"
sentences.n: قولوا لبعضكم بعضا is 'say to one another'. يقول لنا على اسم أمه, 'tell us the name of his mother' (على after قال: 'by way of, concerning'). ابن حرام, 'son of the forbidden', is a bastard. فلم يلعب: lam stands where Classical would use lā, 'so let him not play'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ أَتَوْا إِلَى الْمَكْتَبِ وَحَضَرَ عَجِيبٌ فَأَحَاطَتْ بِهِ الْأَوْلَادُ فَقَالُوا نَحْنُ نَلْعَبُ لُعْبَةً وَلَكِنْ مَا يَلْعَبُ مَعَنَا إِلَّا مَنْ يَقُولُ لَنَا عَلَى اسْمِ أُمِّهِ وَأَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu ataw ilā al-maktabi wa-ḥaḍara ʿajībun fa-aḥāṭat bihi al-awlādu fa-qālū naḥnu nalʿabu luʿbatan wa-lākin mā yalʿabu maʿanā illā man yaqūlu lanā ʿalā ismi ummihi wa-abīhi
sentences.l: And-when became the-morning morning, they-came to the-school, and-ʿAjīb attended, and-surrounded with-him the-children, and-they-said: We play a-game, but not plays with-us except he-who says to-us upon the-name-of his-mother and-his-father.
sentences.i: When morning came they went to the school, and ʿAjīb arrived; the boys crowded around him and said, "We are playing a game, but no one plays with us unless he can tell us the name of his mother and his father."

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ فَقَالَ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمْ اسْمِي مَاجِدٌ وَأُمِّي عَلَوِيَّهْ وَ أَبِي عِزُّالدِّينِ وَقَالَ الْآخَرُ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِ وَالْآخَرُ كَذَلِكَ إِلَى أَنْ جَاءَ الدَّوْرُ إِلَى عَجِيبٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun fa-qāla wāḥidun minhum ismī mājidun wa-ummī ʿalawiyyah wa-abī ʿizzu al-dīni wa-qāla al-ākharu mithla qawlihi wa-al-ākharu kadhālika ilā an jāʾa al-dawru ilā ʿajībin
sentences.l: And-they-said: By-God, good! And-said one of-them: My-name Mājid, and-my-mother ʿAlawiyya, and my-father ʿIzz al-Dīn. And-said the-other like his-saying, and-the-other likewise, until came the-turn to ʿAjīb.
sentences.i: They said, "By God, good!" Then one of them said, "My name is Mājid, my mother is ʿAlawiyya, and my father is ʿIzz al-Dīn." The next said the like, and the next likewise, until the turn came to ʿAjīb.
sentences.n: علويه is the woman's name ʿAlawiyya, printed with a final ه, and و ابي is printed with a space after the و. الآخر, 'the other', serves here for 'the next one'. طيب, 'good, agreed', is colloquial.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ أَنَا اسْمِي عَجِيبٌ وَأُمِّي سِتُّ الْحُسْنِ وَأَبِي شَمْسُ الدِّينِ الْوَزِيرُ بِمِصْرَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla anā ismī ʿajībun wa-ummī sittu al-ḥusni wa-abī shamsu al-dīni al-wazīru bi-miṣra
sentences.l: And-he-said: I, my-name ʿAjīb, and-my-mother Sitt al-Ḥusn, and-my-father Shams al-Dīn the-vizier in-Egypt.
sentences.i: He said, "My name is ʿAjīb, my mother is Sitt al-Ḥusn, and my father is Shams al-Dīn, the vizier in Egypt."
sentences.n: ʿAjīb names his grandfather, the vizier, as his father; the boys' reply in the next sentence turns on this.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ مَا هُوَ أَبُوكَ فَقَالَ لَهُمْ عَجِيبٌ الْوَزِيرُ أَبِي حَقِيقٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu wa-Allāhi inna al-wazīra mā huwa abūka fa-qāla lahum ʿajībun al-wazīru abī ḥaqīqun
sentences.l: And-they-said to-him: By-God, indeed the-vizier not he is your-father. And-said to-them ʿAjīb: The-vizier my-father, true.
sentences.i: They said to him, "By God, the vizier is not your father." ʿAjīb said to them, "The vizier is my father, truly."
sentences.n: حقيق is probably 'true, real' (perhaps حقيقي without its final yāʾ, or ḥaqīq, 'sure'); the sense is plain. ما هو أبوك: colloquial negation of a nominal sentence with ما + pronoun.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ ضَحِكَتْ عَلَيْهِ الْأَوْلَادُ وَصَفَّقُوا عَلَيْهِ وَقَالُوا مَا يُعْرَفُ لَهُ أَبٌ قُمْ مِنْ عِنْدِنَا فَلَا يَلْعَبُ مَعَنَا إِلَّا مَنْ يَعْرِفُ اسْمَ أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika ḍaḥikat ʿalayhi al-awlādu wa-ṣaffaqū ʿalayhi wa-qālū mā yuʿrafu lahu abun qum min ʿindinā fa-lā yalʿabu maʿanā illā man yaʿrifu isma abīhi
sentences.l: And-at that, laughed upon-him the-children and-clapped upon-him and-said: Not is-known for-him a-father! Get-up from by-us! For-not plays with-us except he-who knows the-name-of his-father.
sentences.i: At that the boys laughed at him and clapped their hands at him, and said, "He has no known father! Get up and go from us; no one plays with us unless he knows his father's name."
sentences.n: ضحكت عليه, 'laughed at him', and صفقوا عليه, 'clapped at him', use على for the target of mockery. The edition prints الأولاد here with a precomposed hamza; it is kept.

sentences.t: وَفِى الْحَالِ تَفَرَّقَتِ الْأَوْلَادُ مِنْ حَوْلِهِ وَتَضَا حَكُوا عَلَيْهِ فَضَاقَ صَدْرُهُ وَانْخَنَقَ بِالْبُكَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī al-ḥāli tafarraqati al-awlādu min ḥawlihi wa-taḍā ḥakū ʿalayhi fa-ḍāqa ṣadruhu wa-inkhanaqa bi-al-bukāʾi
sentences.l: And-in the-moment dispersed the-children from around-him, and-laughed-together [taḍā ḥakū] upon-him; and-narrowed his-chest, and-he-choked with-the-weeping.
sentences.i: At once the boys scattered from around him and laughed at him together, so that his heart grew tight and he choked with weeping.
sentences.n: تضا حكوا is one word, تَضَاحَكُوا, 'they laughed together (at him)', split by a stray space in the print; the vocalisation keeps the split. ضاق صدره, 'his chest narrowed', is to be distressed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْعَرِيفُ نَعْرِفُ جَدَّكَ الْوَزِيرَ أَبُو أُمِّكَ سِتِّ الْحُسْنِ لَا أَبُوكَ وَأَمَّا أَبُوكَ فَلَا تَعْرِفُهُ أَنْتَ وَلَا نَحْنُ لِأَنَّ السُّلْطَانَ كَانَ زَوَّجَهَا لِلْأَحْدَبِ السَّائِسِ وَجَاءَتِ الْجِنُّ نَامُوا عِنْدَهَا وَلَا لَكَ أَبٌ يُعْرَفُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-ʿarīfu naʿrifu jaddaka al-wazīra abū ummika sitti al-ḥusni lā abūka wa-ammā abūka fa-lā taʿrifuhu anta wa-lā naḥnu li-anna al-sulṭāna kāna zawwajahā li-al-aḥdabi al-sāʾisi wa-jāʾati al-jinnu nāmū ʿindahā wa-lā laka abun yuʿrafu
sentences.l: And-said to-him the-monitor: We-know your-grandfather the-vizier, father-of your-mother Sitt al-Ḥusn, not your-father. And-as-for your-father, not you-know-him, you, and-not we, because the-sultan had-married-her to-the-hunchback the-groom, and-came the-jinn, they-slept at-her; and-not for-you a-father who-is-known.
sentences.i: The monitor said to him, "We know your grandfather the vizier, the father of your mother Sitt al-Ḥusn; he is not your father. As for your father, neither do you know him nor do we; for the sultan had married her to the hunchbacked groom, and the jinn came and slept with her; so you have no father who is known."
sentences.n: أبو أمك keeps the nominative -ū in apposition where Classical would have أبي. جاءت الجن ناموا: the verb is first feminine singular, then plural. The story's hunchbacked groom and the jinn are the reader's earlier acquaintances; the boys' version of events is a garbled rumour.

sentences.t: وَلَا بَقِيتَ أَنْتَ تَقِيسُ صِغَارَ الْمَكْتَبِ دُونَ أَنْ تَعْرِفَ لَكَ أَبًا :وَإِلَّابَقِيتَ بَيْنَهُمْ وَلَدَزِنًا
sentences.tr: wa-lā baqīta anta taqīsu ṣighāra al-maktabi dūna an taʿrifa laka aban wa-illā baqīta baynahum walada zinan
sentences.l: And-not you-remained, you, measuring the-small-ones-of the-school without that you-know for-you a-father; and-if-not you-remained among-them a-child-of fornication.
sentences.i: "And you must not go on pitting yourself against the little ones of the school without knowing a father of your own; or else you will stay among them a bastard."
sentences.n: تقيس is obscure; perhaps 'measure yourself against, vie with' (from قاس), perhaps a miswriting. ولا بقيت may be a prohibitive formula, 'may you not remain'. والابقيت is وإلا بقيت, 'and if not, you would remain', with the space lost, and ولدزنا is ولد زنا, 'child of fornication', one word; the colon is the print's.

sentences.t: أَلَاتَرَٰي أَنَّ ابْنَ الْبَيَّاعِ يُعْرَفُ بِأَبِيهِ وَأَنْتَ جَدُّكَ وَزِيرُ مِصْرَ وَأَمَّا أَبُوكَ فَلَا نَعْرِفُهُ وَنَحْنُ نَقُولُ مَالَكَ أَبٌ فَاصْحَ لِعَقْلِكَ
sentences.tr: a-lā tarā anna ibna al-bayyāʿi yuʿrafu bi-abīhi wa-anta jadduka wazīru miṣra wa-ammā abūka fa-lā naʿrifuhu wa-naḥnu naqūlu mā laka abun fa-iṣḥa li-ʿaqlika
sentences.l: Do-you-not see that the-son-of the-seller is-known by-his-father, while-you, your-grandfather is-vizier-of Egypt; and-as-for your-father, we-do-not-know-him, and-we say: You-have no father. So-wake-up for-your-mind.
sentences.i: Do you not see that even a pedlar's son is known by his father, while you, your grandfather is the vizier of Egypt; but your father we do not know, and we say you have none. So come to your senses!
sentences.n: الاتري is أَلَا تَرَى, 'do you not see', one word in the print. اصح لعقلك, 'wake up to your mind', is 'come to your senses' (from صحا, 'be sober').

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْعَرِيفِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ وَ تَعْيِيرَهُمْ لَهُ قَامَ مِنْ سَاعَتِهِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى وَالِدَتِهِ سِتِّ الْحُسْنِ وَشَكَى لَهَا وَهُوَ يَبْكِي وَمَنَعَهُ الْبُكَاءُ مِنَ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa mina al-ʿarīfi wa-al-awlādi hādhā al-kalāma wa-taʿyīrahum lahu qāma min sāʿatihi wa-dakhala ʿalā wālidatihi sitti al-ḥusni wa-shakā lahā wa-huwa yabkī wa-manaʿahu al-bukāʾu mina al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And-when he-heard from the-monitor and-the-children this the-speech and their-taunting of-him, he-rose from his-hour and-entered upon his-mother Sitt al-Ḥusn, and-complained to-her, while-he weeps, and-prevented-him the-weeping from the-speech.
sentences.i: When he had heard this talk from the monitor and the boys, and their taunting of him, he got up at that very hour, went in to his mother Sitt al-Ḥusn, and complained to her, weeping, so that his weeping kept him from speaking.
sentences.n: شكى is printed for شكا, 'he complained'. من ساعته, 'from his hour', is 'at once'. دخل على, 'went in to', is the usual way to enter a person's presence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ أُمُّهُ كَلَامَهُ وَبُكَاءَهُ الْتَهَبَ قَلْبُهَا بِالنَّارِ عَلَيْهِ وَقَالَتْ يَا وَلَدِي مَا الَّذِي أَبْكَاكَ فَاحْكِ لِي قِصَّتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat ummuhu kalāmahu wa-bukāʾahu iltahaba qalbuhā bi-al-nāri ʿalayhi wa-qālat yā waladī mā alladhī abkāka fa-iḥki lī qiṣṣataka
sentences.l: And-when heard his-mother his-speech and-his-weeping, her-heart caught-fire with-the-fire upon-him; and-she-said: O my-son, what that-which made-you-weep? So-relate to-me your-story.
sentences.i: When his mother heard his words and his weeping, her heart blazed with grief for him, and she said, "My son, what has made you weep? Tell me your story."
sentences.n: التهب قلبها بالنار عليه, 'her heart took fire with fire over him', is a stock phrase for a mother's anguish; على after a feeling is 'for the sake of, over'.

sentences.t: فَحَكَى لَهَا عَجِيبٌ مَا سَمِعَهُ مِنَ الْأَوْلَادِ وَمِنَ الْعَرِيفِ ثُمَّ مَنْ هُوَيَا وَالِدَتِي أَبِي
sentences.tr: fa-ḥakā lahā ʿajībun mā samiʿahu mina al-awlādi wa-mina al-ʿarīfi thumma man huwa yā wālidatī abī
sentences.l: And-he-related to-her, ʿAjīb, what he-heard from the-children and from the-monitor; then: Who is-he, O my-mother, my-father?
sentences.i: And ʿAjīb told her what he had heard from the boys and from the monitor, and then asked, "Who, mother, is my father?"
sentences.n: هويا is هو يا run together. ثم من هو ... ابي is the boy's own question, slipping into direct speech with no 'and he said'.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ لَهُ أَبُوكَ :وَزِبْرُ مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: qālat lahu abūka wazibru miṣra
sentences.l: She-said to-him: Your-father, vizier-of Egypt.
sentences.i: She said to him, "Your father is the vizier of Egypt."
sentences.n: وزبر is printed for وزير, 'vizier' (ب for ي); it is vocalised as printed and read wazīr. The colon is the print's.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا لَا تَكْذِبِي عَلَيَّ فَإِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَبَاكِ أَنْتِ لَا أَنَا فَمَنْ هُوَ أَبِي فَإِنْ لَمْ تُخْبِرِينِي بِالصَّحِيحِ وَإِلَّا قَتَلْتُ رُوحِي بِهَذَا :الْخَنْجَزِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā lā takdhibī ʿalayya fa-inna al-wazīra abāki anti lā anā fa-man huwa abī fa-in lam tukhbirīnī bi-al-ṣaḥīḥi wa-illā qataltu rūḥī bi-hādhā al-khanjazi
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her: Do-not lie upon-me! For-indeed the-vizier your-father, you, not I. So who is-he, my-father? And-if not you-inform-me with-the-true, and-if-not I-killed my-soul with this the-dagger.
sentences.i: Then he said to her, "Do not lie to me! The vizier is your father, not mine. So who is my father? If you will not tell me the truth, I will kill myself with this dagger!"
sentences.n: The vizier is called أباك, with the accusative ending that has become fixed, 'your father'. إن لم ... وإلا is a doubled 'if not ... and if not'; the perfect قتلت is a firm threat, 'I have killed myself'. الخنجز is printed for الخنجر, 'dagger' (ز for ر). روحي, 'my soul', means 'myself'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ وَالِدَتُهُ ذِكْرَ أَبِيهِ، بَكَتْ لِلذِّكْرِ وَلَدِ عَمِّهَا وَتَذَكَّرَتْ جِلَاهَا عَلَى بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ الْبَصْرِيِّ وَمَاجَرَٰي لَهَا مَعَهُ وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat wālidatuhu dhikra abīhi bakat li-al-dhikri waladi ʿammihā wa-tadhakkarat jilāhā ʿalā badri al-dīni ḥasanin al-baṣriyyi wa-mā jarā lahā maʿahu wa-anshadat taqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And-when heard his-mother the-mention-of his-father, she-wept at-the-mention, the-son-of her-uncle, and-remembered her-unveiling to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan the-Basran, and-what happened to-her with-him, and-recited, saying, these the-verses.
sentences.i: When his mother heard him speak of his father, she wept at the remembrance of her cousin, and recalled how she had been displayed as a bride to Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan of Basra, and all that had passed between them; and she recited these verses.
sentences.n: للذكر keeps an article that Classical would drop (لذكر): 'at the mention of'. ولد عمها, 'son of her uncle', is her cousin. جلاها is obscure, probably 'her unveiling', the display of the bride (جلوة). وماجري is وما جرى run together.

sentences.t:
اَقَامُوا الْوَجْدَ فِي قَلْبِي وَسَارُوْا * وَقَدْ شَطَتْ بِمَنْ اَهْوَى الدِّيَارُ
وَبَانَ تَجَلُّدِي مِنْ حَيْثُ بَانُوْا * وَفَارَقَنِي وَعَزَّ الاِصْطِبَارُ
وَقَدْ سَارُوْا سَرَى عَنِّي سُرُورِي * وَقَدْ عُلِمَ الْقَرَارُ فَلَا قَرَارُ
وَاَجْرَوْا بِالْفِرَاقِ دُمُوعَ عَيْنِي * فَاَدْ مَعْهَا بِبُعْدِهِمْ غِزَارُ
اِذَا مَا اشْتَقْتُ يَوْمًا اَنْ اَرَاهُمْ * وَطَالَ بِهِمْ حَنِينٌ وَانْتِظَارُ
اَتَمَثَّلُ شَخْصَهُمْ فِي وَسْطِ قَلْبِي * غَرَامٌ وَاشْتِيَاقٌ وَافْتِكَارُ
اَيَا مَنْ ذِكْرُهُمْ :اَضْحَى دِيَارِي * كَمَا حُبَّا لَهُمْ هَوَيْ شِعَارُ
اَحِبَّتَنَا اِلَى كَمْ ذَا التَّمَادِي * وَكَمْ هَذَا التَّبَاعُدُ وَالنِّفَارُ
sentences.tr:
aqāmū al-wajda fī qalbī wa-sārū * wa-qad shaṭat bi-man ahwā al-diyāru
wa-bāna tajalludī min ḥaythu bānū * wa-fāraqanī wa-ʿazza al-iṣṭibāru
wa-qad sārū sarā ʿannī surūrī * wa-qad ʿulima al-qarāru fa-lā qarāru
wa-ajraw bi-al-firāqi dumūʿa ʿaynī * fa-ad maʿhā bi-buʿdihim ghizāru
idhā mā ishtaqtu yawman an arāhum * wa-ṭāla bihim ḥanīnun wa-intiẓāru
atamaththalu shakhṣahum fī wasṭi qalbī * gharāmun wa-ishtiyāqun wa-iftikāru
ayā man dhikruhum aḍḥā diyārī * kamā ḥubbā lahum hawā shiʿāru
aḥibbatanā ilā kam dhā al-tamādī * wa-kam hādhā al-tabāʿudu wa-al-nifāru
sentences.l:
They-set-up the-longing in my-heart and-departed * and-have distant-grown from whom I-love the-abodes.
And-vanished my-fortitude from where they-vanished * and-it-left-me, and-dear-became the-patience.
And-they-departed; went-away from-me my-joy * and-it-is-known the-staying, so-no staying.
And-they-made-flow by-the-parting the-tears-of my-eye * so-ad with-it [perhaps: so its-tears], through-their-distance, (are) copious.
When I-yearn one-day to see-them * and-grows-long for-them longing and-waiting,
I-picture their-figure in the-midst-of my-heart * passion and-yearning and-brooding.
O you-whose their-remembrance has-become my-dwelling * as love-for-them, passion, an-under-garment.
O our-beloved-ones, until how-long this the-persisting * and-how-long this the-distance and-the-aversion.
sentences.i:
They planted longing in my heart and went their way, and the homes of the one I love are now far off.
My fortitude vanished the moment they vanished, it forsook me, and patience has grown rare.
They are gone, and with them my gladness; it is known that there is no abiding now.
Through the parting they made the tears of my eye run, and for their absence they flow in torrents.
Whenever I long one day to see them, and my yearning and my waiting for them grow long,
I picture their figures in the midst of my heart: passion, longing, and anxious thought.
O you whose memory has become my dwelling, as love of them is the garment closest to me,
O our beloved ones, how long this obstinacy, how long this distance and estrangement?
sentences.n: This is a poem of eight lines, pointed in the print. Three spots are unclear, and the print's pointing is kept. In line 4 the print divides the words فَاَدْ مَعْهَا; the sense required is most likely فَأَدْمُعُهَا, "so its tears". In line 7 the colon before اَضْحَى is a stray mark in the print, and كَمَا حُبَّا لَهُمْ هَوَيْ شِعَارُ is obscure and perhaps corrupt: I read it as "as love of them, passion, is my close garment". The poem plays on سَارُوا / سَرَى / سُرُورِي and on قَرَار / فَلَا قَرَارُ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَتْ وَصَرَخَتْ وَكَذَلِكَ وَلَدُهَا
sentences.tr: thumma bakat wa-ṣarakhat wa-kadhālika waladuhā
sentences.l: Then she-wept and-screamed, and-likewise her-son.
sentences.i: Then she wept and cried out, and her son did the same.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهِمَا فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَى بُكَائِهِمَا احْتَرَقَ قَلْبُهُ وَقَالَ مَا يُبْكِيكُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-al-wazīri dakhala ʿalayhimā fa-lammā naẓara ilā bukāʾihimā iḥtaraqa qalbuhu wa-qāla mā yubkīkumā
sentences.l: And-behold, with-the-vizier, he-entered upon-the-two-of-them; and-when he-looked at their-weeping, burned his-heart, and-he-said: What makes-weep-you-two?
sentences.i: And behold, the vizier came in upon them; and when he saw their weeping his heart burned within him, and he said, "What makes you two weep?"
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ: the بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears. The sentence is the vizier Shams al-Dīn's return to his wife and her son.

sentences.t: فَأخْبَرَتْهُ بِمَا اتَّفَقَ لِوَلَدِهَا مَعَ صِغَارِ الْمَكْتَبِ فَبَكَى الْآخَرُ ثُمَّ تَذَكَّرَ أخَاهُ وَمَا اتَّفَقَ لَهُ مَعَهُ وَمَا اتَّفَقَ لِابْنَتِهِ وَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ مَا فِي بَاطِنِ الْأمْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhbaratuhu bi-mā ittafaqa li-waladihā maʿa ṣighāri al-maktabi fa-bakā al-ākharu thumma tadhakkara akhāhu wa-mā ittafaqa lahu maʿahu wa-mā ittafaqa li-ibnatihi wa-lam yaʿlam mā fī bāṭini al-amri
sentences.l: And-she-told-him of-what befell for-her-son with the-small-ones of-the-school; and-wept the-other; then he-remembered his-brother and-what befell to-him with-him, and-what befell for-his-daughter, and-not he-knew what was in the-inside of-the-matter.
sentences.i: She told him what had befallen her son at the hands of the schoolboys, and the other wept too. Then he remembered his brother and all that had passed between them, and what had happened to his own daughter; but he did not know what lay beneath the matter.
sentences.n: الْآخَرُ, "the other", is the vizier himself, weeping after the boy. Note the spelling فَبَكَى الْآخَرُ with the precomposed آ, as printed. The vizier does not yet know that the boy is his brother's son, so he is moved only by what he is told.

sentences.t: فَفِى الْحَالِ قَامَ الْوَزِيرُ وَمَشَى حَتَّى طَلَعَ إِلَى الدِّيوَانِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ وَأخْبَرَهُ بِالْقِصَّةِ وَطَلَبَ مِنْهُ الْأذْنَ بِالسَّفَرِ إِلَى الشَّرْقِ وَيَعْبُرُ مَدِينَةَ الْبَصْرَةِ وَيَسْأَلُ عَنِ ابْنِ أخِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-fī al-ḥāli qāma al-wazīru wa-mashā ḥattā ṭalaʿa ilā al-dīwāni wa-dakhala ʿalā al-maliki wa-akhbarahu bi-al-qiṣṣati wa-ṭalaba minhu al-idhna bi-al-safari ilā al-sharqi wa-yaʿburu madīnata al-baṣrati wa-yasʾalu ʿan ibni akhīhi
sentences.l: So-in the-moment rose the-vizier and-walked until he-went-up to the-divan, and-entered upon the-king, and-informed-him with-the-story, and-asked from-him the-permission for-the-travel to the-east, and-he-crosses the-city of-Basra and-asks about the-son-of his-brother.
sentences.i: At once the vizier rose and went up to the divan, and went in to the king and told him the story. He asked his leave to journey to the east, to pass through the city of Basra and ask after his brother's son.
sentences.n: فَفِي الْحَالِ: the print has ففى with a final ى for ي. The last two verbs, وَيَعْبُرُ and وَيَسْأَلُ, stand in the indicative where Classical would expect a subjunctive after a purpose clause; the text is loose here, and the pointing follows the text. يَسْأَلُ keeps the precomposed أ printed in the edition.

sentences.t: وَطَلَبَ مِنَ السُّلْطَانِ أنْ يَكْتُبَ لَهُ مَرَاسِيمَ لِسَائِرِ الْبِلَادِ أيَّ مَوْضِعٍ وَجَدَ فِيهِ ابْنَ أخِيهِ يَأْخُذُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaba min al-sulṭāni an yaktuba lahu marāsīma li-sāʾiri al-bilādi ayya mawḍiʿin wajada fīhi ibna akhīhi yaʾkhudhuhu
sentences.l: And-he-asked from the-sultan that he-write for-him decrees to-all-of the-lands: wherever-place he-found in-it the-son-of his-brother, he-take-him.
sentences.i: He also asked the sultan to write him decrees addressed to all the lands, so that wherever he found his brother's son he might take him.
sentences.n: أَيَّ مَوْضِعٍ وَجَدَ فِيهِ is "in whatever place he found ...", an accusative of place. يَأْخُذُهُ is the indicative where a Classical writer would use the jussive of a conditional; both يَأْخُذُهُ and سَائِر keep the precomposed hamza seat printed in the edition.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى بَيْنَ يَدَيِ السُّلْطَانِ فَرَقَّ لَهُ قَلْبُهُ وَكَتَبَ لَهُ مَرَاسِيمَ لِسَائِرِ الْأقَالِيمِ وَالْبِلَادِ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā bayna yadayi al-sulṭāni fa-raqqa lahu qalbuhu wa-kataba lahu marāsīma li-sāʾiri al-aqālīmi wa-al-bilādi
sentences.l: Then he-wept between the-two-hands-of the-sultan, so-softened for-him his-heart, and-he-wrote for-him decrees to-all-of the-regions and-the-lands.
sentences.i: Then he wept before the sultan, whose heart was moved for him, and he wrote him decrees to all the provinces and lands.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيِ is "in the presence of", literally "between the two hands of". رَقَّ لَهُ قَلْبُهُ: "his heart softened for him".

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بِذَلِكَ الْوَزِيرُ وَدَعٰي لِلسُّلْطَانِ وَوَدَّعَهُ وَفِي الْحَالِ نَزَلَ وَتَجَهَّزَ لِلسَّفَرِ وَأخَذَ مَايَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ وَبِنْتَهُ وَوَلَدَهُ عَجِيبَ وَسَافَرَ أوَّلَ يَوْمٍ وَثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ وَثَالِثَ يَوْمٍ إىٰ أنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ فَوَجَدَهَا ذَاتَ أشْجَارٍ وَأنْهَارٍ كَمَا قَالَ فِيهَا الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa bi-dhālika al-wazīru wa-daʿā li-al-sulṭāni wa-waddaʿahu wa-fī al-ḥāli nazala wa-tajahhaza li-al-safari wa-akhadha mā yaḥtāju ilayhi wa-bintahu wa-waladahu ʿajība wa-sāfara awwala yawmin wa-thāniya yawmin wa-thālitha yawmin ilā an waṣala ilā madīnati dimashqa fa-wajadahā dhāta ashjārin wa-anhārin ka-mā qāla fīhā al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: So-rejoiced at-that the-vizier, and-prayed for-the-sultan, and-bade-him-farewell; and-in the-moment he-went-down and-made-ready for-the-travel, and-took what he-needs, and-his-daughter and-his-son ʿAjīb; and-journeyed the-first-of day and-the-second-of day and-the-third-of day, until he-arrived at the-city of-Damascus, and-found-it possessor-of trees and-rivers, as said of-it the-poet.
sentences.i: The vizier was glad of it, and he prayed for the sultan and took his leave. At once he went down and made ready for the journey, and took what he needed, with his daughter and his son ʿAjīb. He travelled the first day, the second day, and the third day, until he reached the city of Damascus and found it a place of trees and rivers, as the poet has said of it:
sentences.n: The print has دعي for دَعَا (ي for ا) and اى for إِلَى (the lām is dropped): both are spelling slips of the text, kept as printed and pointed as they are meant. مَايَحْتَاجُ is two words run together, مَا يَحْتَاجُ. The vizier's "son" here is his nephew ʿAjīb, whom he has not yet recognised as his brother's child; the text calls him وَلَدَهُ in the sense "his boy".

sentences.t:
مِنْ بَعْدِ يَوْمِي فِي دِمَشْقَ وَلَيْلَتِي * حَلَفَ الزَّمَانُ بِمِثْلِهَا لَايَغْلَطِ
بِتْنَا وَجِنْحُ اللَّيْلِ فِي غَفَلَاتِهِ * وَالصُّبْحُ مُبْتَسِمٌ بِفَرْعِ اَشْمَطِ
وَالظِّلُّ فِي تِلْكَ :الْغُصُونِ كَاَنَّهُ * دُرٌّ يُصَافِحُهُ النَّسِيمُ فَيَسْقُطِ
وَالطَّيْرُ تَقْرَاُ وَالْغَدِيرُ صَحِيفَةٌ * وَالرِّيحُ تَكْتُبُ وَالْغَمَامُ يُنَقِّطِ
sentences.tr:
min baʿdi yawmī fī dimashqa wa-laylatī * ḥalafa al-zamānu bi-mithlihā lā-yaghlaṭi
bitnā wa-jinḥu al-layli fī ghafalātihi * wa-al-ṣubḥu mubtasimun bi-farʿi ashmaṭi
wa-al-ẓillu fī tilka al-ghuṣūni ka-annahu * durrun yuṣāfiḥuhu al-nasīmu fa-yasquṭi
wa-al-ṭayru taqraʾu wa-al-ghadīru ṣaḥīfatun * wa-al-rīḥu taktubu wa-al-ghamāmu yunaqqiṭi
sentences.l:
After my-day in Damascus and-my-night * swore the-time by-the-like-of-it, it-will-not err.
We-spent-the-night, with-the-wing-of the-night in its-heedlessness * and-the-dawn smiling with-the-lock-of a-grey-haired-one.
And-the-shade in those the-branches as-though-it * pearls the-breeze clasps-hands-with, so-they-fall.
And-the-bird reads, and-the-brook is-a-page * and-the-wind writes, and-the-cloud dots.
sentences.i:
After my day and my night in Damascus, Time swore that its like it would never mistake.
We passed the night while the wing of darkness lay heedless, and the dawn smiled with the lock of a grizzled head.
The shade among those branches seemed pearls, which the breeze greets with a handshake and they fall.
The bird reads, the brook is a page, the wind writes, and the cloud dots the letters.
sentences.n: The pointing is the print's. In line 3 the colon before الْغُصُونِ is a stray mark in the print. لَايَغْلَطِ and يَسْقُطِ, يُنَقِّطِ, أَشْمَطِ end in kasra for the rhyme, the poem's rhyme-vowel. The last line is a conceit: the bird reads, the stream is the page, the wind writes, and the clouds (like a scribe) dot the letters, that is, the raindrops fall as diacritical points.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ الْوَزِيرُ فِي مَيْدَانِ الْحَصَى وَنَصَبَ خِيَامَهُ وَقَالَ لِغِلْمَانِهِ نَأْخُذُ الرَّاحَةَ هُنَا يَوْمَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala al-wazīru fī maydāni al-ḥaṣā wa-naṣaba khiyāmahu wa-qāla li-ghilmānihi naʾkhudhu al-rāḥata hunā yawmayni
sentences.l: So-descended the-vizier in the-field of-the-pebbles, and-pitched his-tents, and-said to-his-lads: We-take the-rest here two-days.
sentences.i: The vizier alighted in the Pebble Field and pitched his tents, and said to his servants, "We shall rest here two days."
sentences.n: مَيْدَانُ الْحَصَى, "the Pebble Field", is a well-known open ground outside Damascus. غِلْمَانٌ (plural of غُلَامٌ) are the young men of the household. نَأْخُذُ الرَّاحَةَ, "we take rest", is a plain way of saying "we shall rest".

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَتِ الْغِلْمَانُ الْمَدِينَةَ لِقَضَاءِ حَوَائِجِهِمْ هَذَا يَبِيعُ وَهَذَا يَشْتَرِي وَهَذَا يَدْخُلُ الْحَمَّامَ وَهَذَا يَدْخُلُ جَامِعَ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ الَّذِي مَا فِى الدُّنْيَا مِثْلُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-dakhalati al-ghilmānu al-madīnata li-qaḍāʾi ḥawāʾijihim hādhā yabīʿu wa-hādhā yashtarī wa-hādhā yadkhulu al-ḥammāma wa-hādhā yadkhulu jāmiʿa banī umayyata alladhī mā fī al-dunyā mithluhu
sentences.l: So-entered the-lads (she-entered) the-city for-the-fulfilling-of their-needs: this-one sells, and-this-one buys, and-this-one enters the-bath, and-this-one enters the-mosque of-sons-of Umayya, which not in the-world its-like.
sentences.i: The servants went into the city to see to their needs: this one selling, that one buying, another going to the bath, another to the Umayyad Mosque, the like of which there is not in the world.
sentences.n: A broken plural such as الْغِلْمَانُ takes a feminine singular verb (دَخَلَتْ) in Classical Arabic, and this text keeps that habit. هَذَا ... وَهَذَا is "one ... another". جَامِعُ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ is the Great Mosque of Damascus.

sentences.t: وَخَرَجَ عَجِيبٌ هُوَ وَخَادِمُهُ وَدَخَلُوا الْمَدِينَةَ يَتَفَرَّجُونَ وَالْخَادِمُ يَمْشِي خَلْفَ عَجِيبٍ بِبَنْبُوتٍ لَوْ ضُرِبَ بِهِ جَمَلٌ مَا تَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-kharaja ʿajībun huwa wa-khādimuhu wa-dakhalū al-madīnata yatafarrajūna wa-al-khādimu yamshī khalfa ʿajībin bi-banbūtin law ḍuriba bihi jamalun mā tāra
sentences.l: And-went-out ʿAjīb, he and-his-servant, and-they-entered the-city, they-stroll-to-see; and-the-servant walks behind ʿAjīb with-a-club: if were-struck with-it a-camel, not it-would-rise.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb went out, he and his servant, and they entered the city to see the sights, the servant walking behind ʿAjīb with a cudgel so heavy that a camel struck with it would never have risen again.
sentences.n: يَتَفَرَّجُونَ is colloquial "to look about for pleasure, to take in the sights". بَنْبُوتٌ is a club or heavy staff (the print has it with a first ب; it may be a form of نَبُّوتٌ). مَا تَارَ is printed with ت where Classical has ث: ثَارَ, "to rise up, to stir".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ أَهْلُ دِمَشْقَ إِلَى عَجِيبٍ وَقَدِّهِ وَاعْتِدَا لِهِ وَبَهَائِهِ وَجَمَالِهِ وَهُوَ غُلَامٌ بَدِيعُ الْجَمَالِ رَخِيمُ الدَّلَالِ أَلْطَفُ مِنْ نَسِيمِ الشَّمَالِ وَأَحْلَى مِنَ الْمَاءِ الزُّلَالِ لِلظَّمْآنِ وَأَلَذُّ مِنَ الْعَافِيَهِ لِصَاحِبِ السَّقَامِ تَبِعَهُ جَمٌّ غَفِيرٌ تَجْرِي وَرَاءَهُ وَتَسْبِقُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ahlu dimashqa ilā ʿajībin wa-qaddihi wa-iʿtidā lihi wa-bahāʾihi wa-jamālihi wa-huwa ghulāmun badīʿu al-jamāli rakhīmu al-dalāli alṭafu min nasīmi al-shamāli wa-aḥlā mina al-māʾi al-zulāli li-al-ẓamʾāni wa-aladhdhu mina al-ʿāfiyahi li-ṣāḥibi al-saqāmi tabiʿahu jammun ghafīrun tajrī warāʾahu wa-tasbiquhu
sentences.l: So-when looked the-people of-Damascus at ʿAjīb, and-his-stature, and-his-evenness (of-form), and-his-radiance, and-his-beauty — and-he a-lad wondrous-of the-beauty, soft-of the-coquetry, gentler than the-breeze of-the-north, and-sweeter than the-water the-sweet-and-fresh for-the-thirsty, and-more-delicious than the-well-being for-the-owner-of the-illness — followed-him a-throng, a-great-one, running behind-him and-outstripping-him.
sentences.i: When the people of Damascus saw ʿAjīb, his stature and the symmetry of his form, his radiance and his beauty (for he was a lad of wondrous beauty and tender grace, gentler than the north breeze, sweeter than cool fresh water to the thirsty, and more welcome than health to the sick), a great throng followed him, running behind him and racing ahead of him.
sentences.n: The print splits one word, اعْتِدَالِهِ "his symmetry, his evenness of form", into اعتدا and له; we vowel the halves as وَاعْتِدَا and لِهِ so that they read as the single word. The description is in rhymed prose: الشَّمَالِ, الزُّلَالِ, السَّقَامِ. تَجْرِي is feminine singular because جَمٌّ غَفِيرٌ, "a great crowd", is a collective. الْعَافِيَهِ is printed with final ه where Classical has ة.

sentences.t: وَقَعَدُوا فِى الطَّرِيقِ حَتَّى يَجِيءَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَيَنْظُرُوهُ إِلَى أَنْ كَانَ بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ وَقَفَ الْعَبْدُ عَلَى دُكَّانِ أَبِيهِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ
sentences.tr: wa-qaʿadū fī al-ṭarīqi ḥattā yajīʾa ʿalayhim wa-yanẓurūhu ilā an kāna bi-al-amri al-muqaddari waqafa al-ʿabdu ʿalā dukkāni abīhi badri al-dīni ḥasanin
sentences.l: And-they-sat in the-road until he-come upon-them and-they-look-at-him, until it-was by-the-matter the-decreed (that) stopped the-servant at the-shop of-his-father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.i: They sat down along the road till he should come by them and they might look at him; until, as fate had decreed, the lad stopped at the shop of his father, Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.n: بِالْأَمْرِ الْمُقَدَّرِ is "by the decreed matter", that is, by destiny. الْعَبْدُ, "the servant", is the narrator's modest way of naming the person whose story he tells, here ʿAjīb; the name بَدْرُالدِّينِ is printed as one word.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ طَلَعَ ذَقْنُهُ وَتَكَامَلَ عَقْلُهُ فِي مُدَّةِ الِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ سَنَةً وَكَانَ قَدْ مَاتَ الطَّبَّاخُ وَأَخَذَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ مَالَهُ وَدُكَّانَهُ لِأَنَّهُ اعْتَرَفَ عِنْدَ الْقُضَاةِ وَالشُّهُودِ أَنَّهُ وَلَدُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad ṭalaʿa dhaqnuhu wa-takāmala ʿaqluhu fī muddati al-ithnay ʿashara sanatan wa-kāna qad māta al-ṭabbākhu wa-akhadha badru al-dīni ḥasanun mālahu wa-dukkānahu li-annahu iʿtarafa ʿinda al-quḍāti wa-al-shuhūdi annahu waladuhu
sentences.l: And-had come-up his-beard and-had-become-complete his-mind in the-period of-the-twelve years; and-had died the-cook, and-took Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan his-wealth and-his-shop, because-he had-acknowledged before the-judges and-the-witnesses that-he his-son.
sentences.i: His beard had grown and his mind had come to its full strength in the course of those twelve years. The cook had died, and Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan had taken over his wealth and his shop, for he had declared before the judges and the witnesses that he was the cook's son.
sentences.n: The pronoun in ذَقْنُهُ is most naturally Badr al-Dīn's: the twelve years have aged and matured him. الِاثْنَيْ عَشَرَ سَنَةً is not Classical: the number carries the article and the masculine form before a feminine noun (Classical would say اثْنَتَيْ عَشْرَةَ سَنَةً). We read what is printed. The cook is the man who adopted Badr al-Dīn and left him the shop; اعْتَرَفَ ... أَنَّهُ وَلَدُهُ means Badr al-Dīn claimed to be the dead cook's son, so that the estate came to him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَ ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمُ وَقَفَ وَلَدُهُ وَالْخَادِمُ عَلَيْهِ فَنَظَرَ إِى وَلَدِهِ عَجِيبٍ فَوَجَدَهُ فِي غَايَةِ الْحُسْنِ فَخَفَقَ فُؤَادُهُ وَحَنَّ الدَّمُ إِلَى الدَّمِ وَ تَعَلَّقَ بِهِ قَلْبُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kāna dhālika al-yawmu waqafa waladuhu wa-al-khādimu ʿalayhi fa-naẓara ilā waladihi ʿajībin fa-wajadahu fī ghāyati al-ḥusni fa-khafaqa fuʾāduhu wa-ḥanna al-damu ilā al-dami wa-taʿallaqa bihi qalbuhu
sentences.l: So-when was that the-day, stood his-son and-the-servant at-him; so-he-looked at his-son ʿAjīb and-found-him in the-utmost-of the-beauty; so-throbbed his-heart, and-yearned the-blood to the-blood, and-clung to-him his-heart.
sentences.i: When that day came, his son and the servant stopped before him. He looked at his son ʿAjīb and found him the height of beauty; his heart throbbed, blood yearned to blood, and his heart clung to the boy.
sentences.n: Here and below the narrator calls ʿAjīb the cook's son and the cook ʿAjīb's father, though neither knows it: the reader is told what the characters are not. إِى is printed for إِلَى (the lam has dropped out), so read it as "to, at". حَنَّ الدَّمُ إِلَى الدَّمِ, "blood yearns to blood", is the saying that kinsmen feel their kinship unaware. A lone و stands at the end of a print line before تَعَلَّقَ; we keep it as a separate word.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ قَدْ طَبَخَ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ مُحَلَّي وَهَاجَتْ فِيهِ الْمَحَبَّةُ الْآلٰهِيَّةُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna qad ṭabakha ḥabba rummānin muḥallā wa-hājat fīhi al-maḥabbatu al-ilāhiyyatu
sentences.l: And-he-had cooked seeds-of pomegranate sweetened, and-was-stirred in-him the-love the-divine.
sentences.i: He had just cooked a dish of sweetened pomegranate seeds, and a divine love stirred within him.
sentences.n: حَبُّ رُمَّانٍ is the seeds (the juicy kernels) of the pomegranate. مُحَلَّي is spelled with ي where we expect مُحَلًّى; it means "sweetened". الْآلٰهِيَّةُ is printed with madda, الآلهية; it stands for الْإِلٰهِيَّةُ, "the divine", and we point it with a dagger alif on the ل to show that.

sentences.t: فَنَادَى وَلَدَهُ عَجِيبَ وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدِي يَا مَنْ مَلَكَ قَلْبِي وَفُؤَادِي وَحَنَّ إِلَيْهِ كَبِدِي هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ عِنْدِي وَتَجْبُرَ قَلْبِي وَتَأْكُلَ مِنْ طَعَامِي
sentences.tr: fa-nādā waladahu ʿajība wa-qāla yā sayyidī yā man malaka qalbī wa-fuʾādī wa-ḥanna ilayhi kabidī hal laka an tadkhula ʿindī wa-tajbura qalbī wa-taʾkula min ṭaʿāmī
sentences.l: So-he-called his-son ʿAjīb and-said: O my-master, O who possessed my-heart and-my-heart-core, and-yearned to-him my-liver, is-there for-you that you-enter at-me, and-mend my-heart, and-eat of my-food?
sentences.i: He called out to his son ʿAjīb and said, "My master, you who have taken possession of my heart and soul, toward whom my very liver yearns, will you not come in to me, mend my heart, and eat of my food?"
sentences.n: عَجِيبَ is printed without the alif of the accusative; we read the name as a bare, uninflected vocative-like form. The liver (كَبِدٌ) is, like the heart, a seat of feeling. هَلْ لَكَ أَنْ ... is "would you care to ..." (literally "is there for you [a wish] that ..."). جَبَرَ قَلْبَهُ, "to set his heart (like a broken bone)", is the usual phrase for consoling and gladdening someone.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَمَعَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالدُّمُوعِ مِنْ غَيْرِ اخْتِيَارِهِ وَافْتَكَرَ مَاكَانَ فِيهِ وَمَاهُوَ فِيهِ تِلْكَ السَّاعَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma damaʿat ʿaynāhu bi-al-dumūʿi min ghayri ikhtiyārihi wa-iftakara mākāna fīhi wa-māhuwa fīhi tilka al-sāʿata
sentences.l: Then wept his-two-eyes with-the-tears from other-than his-choosing, and-he-recalled what-was in-it and-what-he in-it that the-hour.
sentences.i: Then his eyes ran with tears against his will, and he remembered what he had been through and what he was in at that very hour.
sentences.n: مَاكَانَ and مَاهُوَ are each printed as one word: "what was" and "what he is". دَمَعَتْ عَيْنَاهُ بِالدُّمُوعِ, "his eyes wept with tears", is a cognate-style intensification.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ عَجِيبٌ كَلَامَ أَبِيهِ حَنَّ قَلْبُهُ لَهُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ هَذَا الطَّبَّاخَ حَنَّ قَلْبِي لَهُ وَكَأَنَّهُ قَدْ فَارَقَ وَلَدًا لَهُ فَادْخُلْ بِنَا عِنْدَهُ لِنَجْبُرَ قَلْبَهُ وَنَأْكُلَ ضِيَافَتَهُ لَعَلَّ بِفِعْلِنَا مَعَهُ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ شَمْلَنَا بِأَبِينَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa ʿajībun kalāma abīhi ḥanna qalbuhu lahu wa-naẓara ilā al-khādimi wa-qāla lahu inna hādhā al-ṭabbākha ḥanna qalbī lahu wa-ka-annahu qad fāraqa waladan lahu fa-udkhul bi-nā ʿindahu li-najbura qalbahu wa-naʾkula ḍiyāfatahu laʿalla bi-fiʿlinā maʿahu yajmaʿu Allāhu shamlanā bi-abīnā
sentences.l: So-when heard ʿAjīb the-speech of-his-father, yearned his-heart to-him; and-he-looked at the-servant and-said to-him: Indeed this the-cook, yearned my-heart to-him, and-as-if-he had parted-from a-son of-his; so-enter with-us at-him, that-we-mend his-heart and-eat his-hospitality; perhaps through-our-deed with-him will-gather God our-union with-our-father.
sentences.i: When ʿAjīb heard his father's words, his heart went out to him. He looked at the servant and said, "My heart has gone out to this cook, as though he had been parted from a son of his. So take us in to him, that we may mend his heart and eat of his hospitality; perhaps, because of what we do for him, God will gather our family together with our father."
sentences.n: حَنَّ قَلْبُهُ لَهُ, "his heart yearned toward him", repeats the verb of the previous scene. فَادْخُلْ بِنَا is "take us in" (دَخَلَ بِـ, "enter with", with the sense of bringing). In لَعَلَّ بِفِعْلِنَا مَعَهُ يَجْمَعُ اللَّهُ the subject follows the verb after an inserted phrase, as in Classical, while لَعَلَّ is followed directly by a verb, as it is in the colloquial. شَمْلٌ is a "union, a family together"; جَمَعَ شَمْلَهُمْ is "to reunite them".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَادِمُ كَلَامَ عَجِيبٍ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ طَيِّبٌ تَبْقَٰي أَوْلَادَ الْوَزِيرِ وَتَأْكُلُ فِي دُكَّانِ الطَّبَّاخِ أَنَا أَحْجُبُ النَّاسَ عَنْكَ بِهَذِهِ الْعَصَا خَوْفًا مِنْ أَنْ يَنْظُرُوا إِلَيْكَ فَمَا آمَنُ أَنْ تَدْخُلَ إِلَى الدُّكَّانِ أَبَدًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khādimu kalāma ʿajībin qāla wa-Allāhi ṭayyibun tabqā awlāda al-wazīri wa-taʾkulu fī dukkāni al-ṭabbākhi anā aḥjubu al-nāsa ʿanka bi-hādhihi al-ʿaṣā khawfan min an yanẓurū ilayka fa-mā āmanu an tadkhula ilā al-dukkāni abadan
sentences.l: So-when heard the-servant the-speech of-ʿAjīb he-said: By-God! Fine! You-remain sons-of the-vizier and-you-eat in the-shop of-the-cook! I, I-screen the-people from-you with this the-staff, in-fear from that they-look at-you; so-not I-am-safe that you-enter to the-shop ever.
sentences.i: When the servant heard ʿAjīb's words he said, "By God, a fine thing! A vizier's son, and eating in a cook's shop! I am keeping the people off you with this staff for fear they should stare at you, and I shall never feel easy about your going into the shop."
sentences.n: طَيِّبٌ is colloquial "fine!", here sarcastic. تَبْقَٰي is colloquial "you remain, you are", the verb used for "to be" in the dialects, and أَوْلَادَ الْوَزِيرِ (plural) stands in the predicate for the class, "vizier's sons". The final ى of تَبْقَٰي is printed as ي. فَمَا آمَنُ, "I am not safe", is first person of أَمِنَ: "I feel no security that ...".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ كَلَامَ الْخَادِمِ تَعَجَّبَ وَ الْنَفَتَ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ وَدُمُوعُهُ سَالَتْ عَلَٰي خُدُودِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa badru al-dīni ḥasanun kalāma al-khādimi taʿajjaba wa-ilnafata ilā al-khādimi wa-dumūʿuhu sālat ʿalā khudūdihi
sentences.l: So-when heard Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan the-speech of-the-servant he-marvelled and-turned to the-servant, with-his-tears having-flowed upon his-cheeks.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan heard the servant's words he was amazed, and he turned to the servant, his tears running down his cheeks.
sentences.n: النفت is printed for التفت (ن for ت), and a lone و stands at the end of the print line before it; we point the letters as they are, وَ الْنَفَتَ, and read "and he turned". وَدُمُوعُهُ سَالَتْ is a circumstantial clause with wāw ("his tears having flowed"), a very common way of saying "while ...". علي is printed for على, so it carries the dagger alif.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ لِلْخَادِمِ إِنَّ قَلْبِي أَحَبَّهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿajībun li-al-khādimi inna qalbī aḥabbahu
sentences.l: So-said ʿAjīb to-the-servant: Indeed my-heart has-loved-him.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb said to the servant, "My heart has taken to him."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ دَعْنَا مِنْ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ وَلَا تَدْخُلْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu al-khādimu daʿnā min hādhā al-kalāmi wa-lā tadkhul
sentences.l: So-said to-him the-servant: Leave-us from this the-speech, and-not enter!
sentences.i: The servant said to him, "Enough of this talk, and do not go in."
sentences.n: دَعْنَا مِنْ ... is colloquial "leave off, enough of ...".

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ الْتَفَتَ أَبُو عَجِيبٍ لِلْخَادِمِ وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا كَبِيرُ لَايْشْ مَاتَجْبُرُ خَاطِرِي وَ تَدْخُلُ عِنْدِي يَا مَنْ كَأَنَّهُ قَسْطَلٌ أَسْوَدُ وَقَلْبُهُ أَبْيَضُ يَا مَنْ قَالَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ وَاصِفِيهِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika iltafata abū ʿajībin li-al-khādimi wa-qāla lahu yā kabīru lāysh mātajburu khāṭirī wa-tadkhulu ʿindī yā man ka-annahu qasṭalun aswadu wa-qalbuhu abyaḍu yā man qāla fīhi baʿḍu wāṣifīhi
sentences.l: So at that turned the-father-of ʿAjīb to-the-servant and-said to-him: O elder! why not-you-mend my-mind and-you-enter at-me? O who as-if-he a-qasṭal black, and-his-heart white! O who said about-him some-one-of his-describers:
sentences.i: At that the father of ʿAjīb turned to the servant and said, "Elder, why will you not set my mind at ease and come in to me? You who are like a black qasṭal with a heart of white, you of whom one of your describers has said:"
sentences.n: لَايْشْ is the Egyptian-Syrian colloquial "why?" (from لِأَيِّ شَيْءٍ), and مَاتَجْبُرُ is the colloquial negative of the present (مَا + imperfect): "why do you not ...". يَا كَبِيرُ, "O elder", is a polite address to the eunuch. قَسْطَلٌ is obscure here; the picture of something black outside and white within suggests a chestnut, but we are not sure of the word. The father alludes to the black eunuch's white heart in the verses that follow.

sentences.t: فَضَحِكَ الْخَادِمُ وَقَالَ أَيْشْ قُلْتَ فَبِاللَّهِ قُلْ وَأَوْجِزْ فَفِى الْحَالِ أَنْشَدَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-ḍaḥika al-khādimu wa-qāla aysh qulta fa-bi-Allāhi qul wa-awjiz fa-fī al-ḥāli anshada badru al-dīni ḥasanun wa-jaʿala yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So-laughed the-servant and-said: What you-said? So-by-God, say and-be-brief! So-at the-moment recited Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, and-began he-says these the-verses:
sentences.i: The servant laughed and said, "What did you say? By God, say it, and be brief." At once Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan recited, and began to say these verses:
sentences.n: أَيْشْ is colloquial "what?" (from أَيُّ شَيْءٍ). فَبِاللَّهِ is an oath-phrase, "in God's name": here it urges, "for God's sake, say it". فَفِى الْحَالِ is "at once". جَعَلَ يَقُولُ is "began to say".

sentences.t:
لَوْلَا تَأَدُّبُهُ وَحُسْنُ ثِقَاتِهِ * مَا كَانَ فِي دَارِ الْمُلُوكِ مُحَكَّمَا
وَعَلَى الْحَرِيمِ فَيَالَهُ مِنْ خَادِمٍ * مِنْ حُسْنِهِ خَدَمَتْهُ أَمْلَاكُ السَّمَا
sentences.tr:
law-lā taʾaddubuhu wa-ḥusnu thiqātihi * mā kāna fī dāri al-mulūki muḥakkaman
wa-ʿalā al-ḥarīmi fa-yālahu min khādimin * min ḥusnihi khadamathu amlāku al-samā
sentences.l: Were-it-not-for his-good-breeding and-the-goodness-of his-trustworthiness, not he-would-be in the-house of-the-kings given-authority; and-over the-harem — O-for-him, what-a servant! — from his-goodness served-him the-angels-of the-heaven.
sentences.i: But for his good breeding and the excellence of his trust, he would never be set in authority in the house of kings; and over the harem, what a servant! For his goodness the very angels of heaven would wait upon him.
sentences.n: The edition prints this verse with its marks, and we keep them exactly. The words are "the angels of heaven served him" because of his goodness; السَّمَا is السَّمَاءِ with the hamza dropped, as the metre and rhyme need. ثِقَاتِهِ is an odd form (the plural of ثِقَةٍ, "trusted ones"); it may be a slip for ثَقَافَتِهِ, "his cultivation", but we leave it as printed and read "his trustworthiness". فَيَالَهُ مِنْ خَادِمٍ is an exclamation: "what a servant he is!". مُحَكَّمًا is "given authority, made judge".

sentences.t: فَتَعَجَّبَ الْخَادِمُ مِنْ هَذَا الْكَلَامِ وَأَخَذَ عَجِيبًا وَدَخَلَ دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ فَغَرَفَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ زُبْدِيَّةَ حَبِّ رُمَّانٍ عَالِيَةً وَكَانَتْ بِلَوْزٍ وَسُكَّرٍ فَأَكَلُوا سَوَاءً
sentences.tr: fa-taʿajjaba al-khādimu min hādhā al-kalāmi wa-akhadha ʿajīban wa-dakhala dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi fa-gharafa badru al-dīni ḥasanun zubdiyyata ḥabbi rummānin ʿāliyatan wa-kānat bi-lawzin wa-sukkarin fa-akalū sawāʾan
sentences.l: So-marvelled the-servant at this the-speech, and-took ʿAjīb and-entered the-shop of-the-cook; so-ladled Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan a-bowl-of seeds-of pomegranate, excellent, and-it-was with-almonds and-sugar; so-they-ate together.
