sentences.i: The servant marvelled at these words; he took ʿAjīb and went into the cook's shop, and Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan ladled out a superb bowl of pomegranate seeds, made with almonds and sugar, and they ate together.
sentences.n: زُبْدِيَّةٌ is a deep bowl (the word is also used of a dish of food). عَالِيَةً is colloquial "top-quality". بِلَوْزٍ وَسُكَّرٍ is "with almonds and sugar": the bi- here marks what the dish is made with. سَوَاءً is "alike, together, all on an equal footing".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ آنَسْتُمُونَا فَكُلُوا هَنِيأً مَرِيئًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum badru al-dīni ḥasanun ānastumūnā fa-kulū hanīʾan marīʾan
sentences.l: So-said to-them Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: You-have-given-us-company! so-eat wholesomely, healthfully.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said to them, "You have given us your company; now eat, and may it do you good."
sentences.n: آنَسْتُمُونَا is the verb آنَسَ, "to keep company, to be friendly to". هَنِيأً مَرِيئًا, "wholesomely, healthfully" (a pair of adverbs, "may it be pleasant and agreeable to you"), is the usual wish said to those who eat. Both words are printed with their own hamza; we keep it as printed.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَجِيبًا قَالَ لِوَالِدِهِ اقْعُدْ كُلْ مَعَنَا لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَجْمَعُنَا بِمَنْ نُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ʿajīban qāla li-wālidihi uqʿud kul maʿanā laʿalla Allāha yajmaʿunā bi-man nurīdu
sentences.l: Then indeed ʿAjīb said to-his-father: Sit, eat with-us; perhaps God will-gather-us with-whom we-want.
sentences.i: Then ʿAjīb said to his father, "Sit down and eat with us; perhaps God will bring us together with the one we seek."
sentences.n: اقْعُدْ كُلْ is two commands set side by side with no wa-: "sit, eat". كُلْ is the imperative of أَكَلَ. جَمَعَ ... بِـ is "to bring together with".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ يَا وَلَدِي عَلَى صِغَرِ سِنِّكَ بُلِيتَ بِفُرْقَةِ الْأَحْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun yā waladī ʿalā ṣighari sinnika bulīta bi-furqati al-aḥbābi
sentences.l: So-said Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: O my-son, upon smallness-of your-age you-were-afflicted with-the-parting-of the-loved-ones.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "My son, young as you are, you have been afflicted with parting from those you love."
sentences.n: عَلَى صِغَرِ سِنِّكَ is "despite your small age" (ʿalā here means "in spite of"). بُلِيتَ بِـ is "you have been tried with", and the passive verb takes بِـ for the affliction.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ نَعَمْ يَا عَمِّ احْتَرَقَ قَلْبِي بِفِرَاقِ الْأَحْبَابِ وَهُوَ وَالِدِي وَقَدْ خَرَجْتُ أَنَا وَجَدِّي نَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِ الْبِلَادَ فَوَاحَسْرَتَاهُ عَلَى جَمْعِ شَمْلِي وَبَكَى بُكَاءً شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿajībun naʿam yā ʿammi iḥtaraqa qalbī bi-firāqi al-aḥbābi wa-huwa wālidī wa-qad kharajtu anā wa-jaddī naṭūfu ʿalayhi al-bilāda fa-wā-ḥasratāhu ʿalā jamʿi shamlī wa-bakā bukāʾan shadīdan
sentences.l: So-said ʿAjīb: Yes, O uncle! burned my-heart with-the-separation-from the-loved-ones — and-he my-father — and-I-went-out, I and-my-grandfather, we-go-round for-him the-lands; so-O-my-grief for the-gathering-of my-union! And-he-wept a-weeping severe.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb said, "Yes, uncle. My heart is burned with parting from one I love, and he is my father. I set out, my grandfather and I, to go round the lands in search of him. Oh, my grief, to see my family together again!" And he wept bitterly.
sentences.n: نَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِ الْبِلَادَ is "we go round the lands for him" (طَافَ عَلَى, "to go round in search of"), with the present tense used for the ongoing journey. فَوَاحَسْرَتَاهُ is the cry "O, my grief!" (the wāw is the exclamatory wā). عَلَى جَمْعِ شَمْلِي, "for the gathering of my union", means "to be reunited". The grandfather is the vizier.

sentences.t: فَبَكَى وَالِدُهُ لِفِرَاقِهِ وَبُكَاءِهِ وَتَذَكَّرَ فُرْقَةَ الْأَحْبَابِ وَبُعْدَهُ عَنْ وَالِدِهِ وَوَالِدَتِهِ فَحَزِنَ لَهُ الْخَادِمُ وَأَكَلُوا جَمِيعًا إِلَى أَنِ اكْتَفَوْا
sentences.tr: fa-bakā wāliduhu li-firāqihi wa-bukāʾihi wa-tadhakkara furqata al-aḥbābi wa-buʿdahu ʿan wālidihi wa-wālidatihi fa-ḥazina lahu al-khādimu wa-akalū jamīʿan ilā an iktafaw
sentences.l: So-wept his-father at-his-parting and-his-weeping, and-he-remembered the-parting-of the-loved-ones and-his-distance from his-father and-his-mother; so-grieved for-him the-servant; and-they-ate all-together until they-were-satisfied.
sentences.i: His father wept at the boy's parting and at his weeping, and remembered the separation of loved ones, and his own distance from his father and mother; the servant too was grieved for him, and they all ate together until they were full.
sentences.n: وَالِدُهُ, "his father", is the cook, as the narrator tells us again. The two pronouns in لِفِرَاقِهِ وَبُكَاءِهِ are ʿAjīb's. The same word, وَالِدِهِ, then names Badr al-Dīn's own father, and the pronoun in بُعْدَهُ is Badr al-Dīn's.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ قَامُوا خَرَجُوا مِنْ دُكَّانِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ فَحَسَّ أَنَّ رُوحَهُ فَارَقَتْ جَسَدَهُ وَرَاحَتْ مَعَهُمْ فَمَا قَدَرَ يَصْبِرُ عَنْهُمْ لَحْظَةً وَاحِدَةً فَقَفَلَ الدُّكَّانَ وَتَبِعَهُمْ وَهُوَ لَايَعْلَمُ أَنَّهُ وَالِدُهُ وَأَسْرَعَ فِي مَشْيِهِ حَتَّى لَحِقَهُمْ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنَ الْبَابِ الْكَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: thumma baʿda dhālika qāmū kharajū min dukkāni badri al-dīni ḥasanin fa-ḥassa anna rūḥahu fāraqat jasadahu wa-rāḥat maʿahum fa-mā qadara yaṣbiru ʿanhum laḥẓatan wāḥidatan fa-qafala al-dukkāna wa-tabiʿahum wa-huwa lāyaʿlamu annahu wāliduhu wa-asraʿa fī mashyihi ḥattā laḥiqahum qabla an yakhrujū mina al-bābi al-kabīri
sentences.l: Then after that they-rose, they-went-out from the-shop of-Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan; and-he-felt that his-spirit had-left his-body and-gone with-them; so-not he-was-able he-endures apart-from-them a-moment one; so-he-locked the-shop and-followed-them, and-he not-knowing that-he his-father; and-hastened in his-walking until he-overtook-them before that they-go-out from the-gate the-great.
sentences.i: Then they got up and went out of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan's shop, and he felt that his spirit had left his body and gone off with them; he could not bear to be without them for a single moment. So he locked up the shop and followed them, not knowing that he was the boy's father, and hurried on until he caught up with them, before they could go out of the great gate.
sentences.n: قَامُوا خَرَجُوا is two verbs side by side with no wa-: "they rose and went out". حَسَّ is colloquial "to feel, to sense". رَاحَتْ is "went away", and فَمَا قَدَرَ يَصْبِرُ is the colloquial "he could not (bring himself to) endure", where a bare imperfect follows قَدَرَ. قَفَلَ is colloquial "to lock". In أَنَّهُ وَالِدُهُ the "he" is Badr al-Dīn and "his" is the boy's: he does not know that he is ʿAjīb's father. الْبَابُ الْكَبِيرُ is one of Damascus's main gates.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ الطَّوَاشِيُّ وَقَالَ لَهُ مَالَكَ فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ لَمَّا نَزَلْتُمْ مِنْ عِنْدِي حَسِيتُ أَنَّ رُوحِي رَاحَتْ مَعَكُمْ وَلِي حَاجَةٌ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ خَارِجَ الْبَابِ فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أُرَافِقَكُمْ حَتَّٰي أَقْضِيَ حَاجَتِي وَأَرْجِعَ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata al-ṭawāshiyyu wa-qāla lahu mālaka fa-qāla badru al-dīni ḥasanun lammā nazaltum min ʿindī ḥasaytu anna rūḥī rāḥat maʿakum wa-lī ḥājatun fī al-madīnati khārija al-bābi fa-aradtu an urāfiqakum ḥattā aqḍiya ḥājatī wa-arjiʿa
sentences.l: So-turned the-eunuch and-said to-him: What-to-you? So-said Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan: When you-went-down from at-me, I-felt that my-spirit had-gone with-you; and-for-me a-need in the-city outside the-gate, so-I-wanted that I-accompany-you until I-fulfil my-need and-return.
sentences.i: The eunuch turned and said to him, "What is the matter with you?" Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan said, "When you left my shop I felt that my spirit had gone with you, and I have an errand in the city beyond the gate, so I wished to go along with you until I have done my errand and can return."
sentences.n: مَالَكَ is printed as one word: "what is the matter with you?" (literally "what for you?"). الطَّوَاشِيُّ is the eunuch, the same man as الْخَادِمُ. حَسِيتُ is the colloquial "I felt" (Classical حَسَسْتُ). خَارِجَ الْبَابِ is "outside the gate"; حَاجَةٌ is "a need, an errand".

sentences.t: فَغَضِبَ الطَّوَاشِيُّ وَقَالَ لِعَجِيبٍ كُنْتُ خَائِفًا مِنْ هَذَا أَكَلْنَا لُقْمَةً كَانَتْ مَشُومَةً وَصَارَ عَلَيْنَا مَكْرُمَةً وَهَاهُوَ تَابِعُنَا مِنْ مَوْضِعٍ إِلَى مَوْضِعٍ
sentences.tr: fa-ghaḍiba al-ṭawāshiyyu wa-qāla li-ʿajībin kuntu khāʾifan min hādhā akalnā luqmatan kānat mashūmatan wa-ṣāra ʿalaynā makrumatan wa-hāhuwa tābiʿunā min mawḍiʿin ilā mawḍiʿin
sentences.l: So-grew-angry the-eunuch and-said to-ʿAjīb: I-was fearing from this; we-ate a-morsel, it-was ill-omened, and-it-became upon-us an-obligation-of-courtesy; and-here-he following-us from place to place.
sentences.i: The eunuch grew angry and said to ʿAjīb, "I was afraid of this. We ate a morsel, and it was an ill-omened one, and it has put us under an obligation; and now see, he is following us from place to place!"
sentences.n: لُقْمَةٌ is a single mouthful. مَشُومَةٌ is "ill-omened". مَكْرُمَةً is an act of generosity; here, a favour that we now owe, though the exact sense is uncertain. وَهَاهُوَ is "and here he is". تَابِعُنَا is the active participle with a suffix, "he who follows us".

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ عَجِيبٌ فَلَقِيَ الطَّبَّاخَ خَلْفَهُ فَاغْتَاظَ وَاحْمَرَّ وَجْهُهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْخَادِمِ دَعْهُ يَمْشِي فِي طَرِيقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَإِذَا خَرَجْنَا إِلَى خِيَامِنَا وَعَرَفْنَا أَنَّهُ تَبِعَنَا نَطْرُدُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata ʿajībun fa-laqiya al-ṭabbākha khalfahu fa-aghtāẓa wa-aḥmarra wajhuhu thumma qāla li-al-khādimi daʿhu yamshī fī ṭarīqi al-muslimīna qa-idhā kharajnā ilā khiyāminā wa-ʿarafnā annahu tabiʿanā naṭruduhu
sentences.l: So-turned ʿAjīb and-met the-cook behind-him; so-he-was-enraged and-reddened his-face. Then he-said to-the-servant: Leave-him, he-walks in the-road of-the-Muslims; and-if we-have-gone-out to our-tents and-we-know that-he followed-us, we-drive-him-off.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb turned and found the cook behind him, and he was enraged, his face turned red. Then he said to the servant, "Leave him; he is walking on the Muslims' road. If we get out to our tents and find that he has followed us, we shall drive him off."
sentences.n: قَإِذَا is printed with ق, an evident slip for فَإِذَا ("and when"); we point the letters as they stand. دَعْهُ يَمْشِي is "leave him walking", the bare imperfect after the imperative. In نَطْرُدُهُ the main clause has no fa- after the conditional clause: "if ... , we drive him off".

sentences.t: فَأَطْرَقَ رَأْسَهُ وَمَشَى وَالْخَادِمُ وَرَاءَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-aṭraqa raʾsahu wa-mashā wa-al-khādimu warāʾahu
sentences.l: So-he-lowered his-head and-walked, and-the-servant behind-him.
sentences.i: He lowered his head and walked on, the servant behind him.
sentences.n: أَطْرَقَ رَأْسَهُ is "he looked down, he bowed his head"; وَالْخَادِمُ وَرَاءَهُ is a circumstantial clause, "with the servant behind him".

sentences.t: فَتَبِعَهُمْ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ إِلَى مَيْدَانِ الْحَصَى وَقَرُبُوا مِنَ الْخِيَامِ فَالْتَفَتُوا وَرَاءَهُ خَلْفَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-tabiʿahum badru al-dīni ḥasanun ilā maydāni al-ḥaṣā wa-qarubū mina al-khiyāmi fa-iltafatū warāʾahu khalfahum
sentences.l: So-followed-them Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan to the-field of-the-pebbles, and-they-drew-near from the-tents; so-they-turned behind-him, behind-them.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan followed them to the Pebble Field, and when they drew near the tents they turned round, and there he was behind them.
sentences.n: The last two words are two adverbs side by side, وَرَاءَهُ خَلْفَهُمْ, "behind him, behind them"; the sense is simply that they turned and looked behind them, and found him there.

sentences.t: فَغَضِبَ عَجِيبٌ وَخَافَ مِنَ الطَّوَاشِيِّ أَنْ يُخْبِرَ جَدَّهُ فَامْتَزَجَ بِالْغَضَبِ لِئَلَّا يَقُولَ أَنَّهُ دَخَلَ دُكَّانَ الطَّبَّاخِ وَأَنَّ الطَّبَّاخَ تَبِعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-ghaḍiba ʿajībun wa-khāfa mina al-ṭawāshiyyi an yukhbira jaddahu fa-imtazaja bi-al-ghaḍabi li-allā yaqūla annahu dakhala dukkāna al-ṭabbākhi wa-anna al-ṭabbākha tabiʿahu
sentences.l: So-grew-angry ʿAjīb and-feared from the-eunuch that he-inform his-grandfather; so-he-was-mingled with-the-anger, lest he-say that-he entered the-shop of-the-cook and-that the-cook followed-him.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb grew angry, and he feared that the eunuch would tell his grandfather; fear mingled with his fury, lest the man say that he had gone into the cook's shop and that the cook had followed him.
sentences.n: فَامْتَزَجَ بِالْغَضَبِ is "and he was mingled with anger": his fear and his rage were mixed together. خَافَ مِنْ ... أَنْ is "he feared that ...".

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَ وَوَجَدَ عَيْنَهُ فِي عَيْنِهِ وَهُوَ بَقِيَ جَسَدٌ بِلَارُوحٍ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafata wa-wajada ʿaynahu fī ʿaynihi wa-huwa baqiya jasadun bi-lā rūḥin
sentences.l: So-he-turned and-found his-eye in his-eye, and-he had-become a-body without-spirit.
sentences.i: He turned, and his eye met the cook's eye: the man had become a body without a spirit.
sentences.n: وَجَدَ عَيْنَهُ فِي عَيْنِهِ, "he found his eye in his eye", means their eyes met. بَقِيَ is colloquial "to become", and after it the print gives جَسَد without the alif of the accusative; we read it as a bare, uninflected noun. بِلَارُوحٍ is printed as one word: "without spirit".

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ عَجِيبٌ أَنَّ عَيْنَهُ عَيْنُ خَائِنٍ أَوْيَكُونُ وَلَدُزِنًا فَازْدَادَ غَضَبًا فَأَخَذَ حَجَرًا وَضَرَبَ بِهِ وَالِدَهُ فَوَقَعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ وَسَالَ الدَّمُ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ʿajībun anna ʿaynahu ʿaynu khāʾinin awyakūnu waladuzinan fa-izdāda ghaḍaban fa-akhadha ḥajaran wa-ḍaraba bihi wālidahu fa-waqaʿa badru al-dīni ḥasanun mughshiyyan ʿalayhi wa-sāla al-damu ʿalā wajhihi
sentences.l: So-looked ʿAjīb (and-saw) that his-eye an-eye-of a-traitor, or-it-may-be a-son-of-adultery; so-his-anger-increased; so-he-took a-stone and-struck with-it his-father; so-fell Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan fainted upon-him, and-flowed the-blood upon his-face.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb looked and saw that the man's eye was a traitor's eye, or the eye of a bastard, and his anger grew; he picked up a stone and struck his own father with it, and Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan fell down in a swoon, and the blood ran over his face.
sentences.n: أَوْيَكُونُ is printed as one word: "or it may be that he is", with يَكُونُ used like "perhaps" and a nominative predicate; وَلَدُزِنًا is likewise one word, "son of fornication", a bastard, and a strong insult. وَالِدَهُ again calls the cook ʿAjīb's father: the boy strikes the father he is looking for. مُغْشِيًّا عَلَيْهِ is "in a faint" (literally "covered over upon").

sentences.t: وَسَارَعَجِيبٌ وَالْخَادِمُ إِلَى الْخِيَامِ
sentences.tr: wa-sāra ʿajībun wa-al-khādimu ilā al-khiyāmi
sentences.l: And-went ʿAjīb and-the-servant to the-tents.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb and the servant went off to the tents.
sentences.n: وَسَارَعَجِيبٌ is printed as one word: وَسَارَ عَجِيبٌ, "and ʿAjīb went". ʿAjīb is the boy whom Badr al-Dīn has been chasing.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا أَفَاقَ مَسَحَ دَمَهُ وَقَطَعَ قِطْعَةً مِنْ عِمَامَتِهِ وَعَصَبَ رَأْسَهُ وَلَامَ نَفْسَهُ وَقَالَ أَنَا ظَالِمُ الصَّبِيِّ غَلَّقْتُ دُكَّانِي وَتَبِعْتُهُ حَتَّى ظَنَّ أَنِّي خَائِنٌ فَرَجَعَ إِلَى دُكَّانِهِ وَبَاعَ طَعَامَهُ وَصَارَيَتَشَوَّقُ لِوَالِدَتِهِ الَّتِي فِى الْبَصْرَةِ وَيَبْكِي عَلَيْهَا وَأَنْشَدَ :ي — و
sentences.tr: wa-ammā badru al-dīni ḥasanun fa-innahu lammā afāqa masaḥa damahu wa-qaṭaʿa qiṭʿatan min ʿimāmatihi wa-ʿaṣaba raʾsahu wa-lāma nafsahu wa-qāla anā ẓālimu al-ṣabiyyi ghallaqtu dukkānī wa-tabiʿtuhu ḥattā ẓanna annī khāʾinun fa-rajaʿa ilā dukkānihi wa-bāʿa ṭaʿāmahu wa-ṣāra yatashawwaqu li-wālidatihi allatī fī al-baṣrati wa-yabkī ʿalayhā wa-anshada :y — w
sentences.l: And-as-for Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, indeed-he, when he-came-to, wiped his-blood and-cut a-piece from his-turban and-bound his-head, and-blamed his-self, and-said: I (am) a-wronger-of the-boy: I-shut my-shop and-followed-him until he-thought that-I (was) a-traitor. Then-he-returned to his-shop and-sold his-food and-began to-long for-his-mother, who (is) in Basra, and-to-weep over-her, and-recited: [:y — w]
sentences.i: As for Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, when he came to himself he wiped away the blood, cut a strip from his turban and bound up his head, and reproached himself. "I have wronged the boy," he said. "I shut up my shop and went after him, until he took me for a villain." Then he went back to his shop and sold his food, and began to long for his mother in Basra and to weep for her, and he recited:
sentences.n: ظَالِمُ الصَّبِيِّ is "wronger of the boy" (an active participle governing a genitive). After وَأَنْشَدَ the print carries stray marks (:ي — و); they are kept exactly as printed and left unpointed. Read the sentence as ending "and he recited:", with the verses that follow.

sentences.t:
لَاتَسْأَلِ الدَّهْرَ انْصَافاً فَتَظْلِمُهُ * وَلَا تَلُمْهُ فَلَمْ يُخْلَقْ لِانْصَافِ
خُذْ مَا تَيَسَّرَ وَابْقِ الْهَمَّ نَاحِيَةً * لَا بُدَّ مِنْ كَدَرٍ فِيهِ وَمِنْ صَافِ
sentences.tr:
lā tasʾali al-dahra inṣāfan fa-taẓlimuhu * wa-lā talumhu fa-lam yukhlaq li-inṣāfi
khudh mā tayassara wa-abqi al-hamma nāḥiyatan * lā budda min kadarin fīhi wa-min ṣāfi
sentences.l:
Do-not ask the-time for-fairness, so-you-wrong-it, * and-do-not blame-it, for-not it-was-created for-fairness.
Take what has-been-made-easy, and-keep the-worry aside; * no escape from a-turbidity in-it and from a-clear-one.
sentences.i: Ask not of Time for fairness, lest you wrong it; nor blame it, for it was never made for justice. Take what comes easily and keep your care to one side: in life there must be some murk, and some clear water.
sentences.n: The pointing is the edition's own, kept as printed. فَتَظْلِمُهُ is pointed as an indicative; after the فَـ of consequence a subjunctive (فَتَظْلِمَهُ) would be expected. لِانْصَافِ and وَابْقِ lack the printed hamza (read لِإِنْصَافٍ, وَأَبْقِ), and صَافِ stands for صَافٍ with the tanwīn dropped. الدَّهْر, "Time", is the usual Arabic name for fate.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ اسْتَمَرَّ يَبِيعُ فِي طَعَامِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna badra al-dīni ḥasana istamarra yabīʿu fī ṭaʿāmihi
sentences.l: Then indeed Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan continued, he-sells in his-food.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan went on selling his food.
sentences.n: اسْتَمَرَّ يَبِيعُ, "he continued, he sells", is the Arabic way of saying "he went on selling": two verbs side by side, with no "that" between.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْوَزِيرُ عَمُّهُ فَإِنَّهُ أَقَامَ فِي دِمَشْقَ ثَلٰثَةَ أَبَّامٍ ثُمَّ رَحَلَ طَالِبَ حِمْصَ فَدَخَلَ إِلَيْهَا وَفَتَّشَ فِي طَرِيقِهِ أَيْنَمَا حَلَّ وَجْهَهُ فِي سَيْرِهِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى دِيَارِ بَكْرٍوَمَا رْدِينَ وَالْمَوْصِلِ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا إِلَى مَدِينَةِ الْبَصْرَةِ فَدَخَلَ بِهَا فَلَمَّا اسْتَقَرَّ بِهَا الْمَنْزِلُ دَخَلَ إِلَى سُلْطَانِهَا وَاجْتَمَعَ بِهِ فَاحْتَرَمَهُ وَأَكْرَمَ مَنْزِلَهُ وَ سَأَلَهُ عَنْ سَبَبِ مَجِيئِهِ فَأَخْبَرَهُ بِقِصَّتِهِ وَأَنَّ أَخَاهُ الْوَزِيرَ نُورَالدِّينِ عَلِي
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-wazīru ʿammuhu fa-innahu aqāma fī dimashqa thalāthata ayyāmin thumma raḥala ṭāliba ḥimṣa fa-dakhala ilayhā wa-fattasha fī ṭarīqihi aynamā ḥalla wajhuhu fī sayrihi ilā an waṣala ilā diyāri bakrin wa-mārdīna wa-al-mawṣili wa-lam yazal sāʾiran ilā madīnati al-baṣrati fa-dakhala bihā fa-lammā istaqarra bihā al-manzilu dakhala ilā sulṭānihā wa-ijtamaʿa bihi fa-iḥtaramahu wa-akrama manzilahu wa-saʾalahu ʿan sababi majīʾihi fa-akhbarahu bi-qiṣṣatihi wa-anna akhāhu al-wazīra nūra al-dīni ʿalī
sentences.l: And-as-for the-vizier, his-uncle, indeed-he stayed in Damascus three days; then he-set-out seeking Homs and-entered it, and-searched on his-road wherever his-face alighted in his-journey, until he-arrived at the-lands-of Bakr and-Mārdīn and-the-Mosul; and-not he-ceased travelling to the-city-of Basra, and-entered it. And-when the-lodging settled for-him in-it, he-entered to its-sultan and-met with-him, and-he-honoured-him and-honoured his-lodging and-asked-him about the-cause-of his-coming, and-he-informed-him of-his-story and-that his-brother the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī (...)
sentences.i: As for the vizier, his uncle, he stayed three days in Damascus, then set out in search of Homs; he entered it, and made inquiry along his road wherever his course took him, until he came to Diyār Bakr, Mārdīn and Mosul, and went on travelling until he reached the city of Basra and entered it. When he had taken up his lodging there, he went in to its Sultan and met him; the sultan received him with respect and honoured his lodging, and asked him the cause of his coming. He told him his story, and how his brother the vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī (...)
sentences.n: The sentence breaks off after نُورَالدِّينِ عَلِي: the verb ("had died") has dropped out, and the sultan's condolence follows. اَبَّام is a slip for ايام, with ب for ي; it is read ayyām. ثَلٰثَةَ, printed ثلثة, is ثلاثة. The space in بَكْرٍوَمَا رْدِينَ is misplaced: read ديار بكر وماردين, "Diyār Bakr and Mārdīn". اينما حل وجهه, "wherever his face alighted", means wherever he turned. فَدَخَلَ بِهَا, "he entered it", uses بِـ where Classical has a bare object. وَ and سَأَلَهُ are printed apart at a line break.

sentences.t: فَتَرَحَّمَ عَلَيْهِ السُّلْطَانُ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَيُّهَا الصَّاحِبُ كَانَ وَزِيرِي وَكُنْتُ أُحِبُّهُ كَثِيرًا مِنْ مُدَّةِ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً وَمَاتَ وَخَلَّفَ وَلَدًا وَمَا أَقَامَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ إِلَّا شَهْرًا وَاحِدًا وَلَقَدْتَاهَ وَلَمْ نَطَّلِعْ لَهُ عَلَى خَبَرٍ غَيْرَأَنَّ أُمَّهُ عِنْدَنَا لِأَنَّهَا بِنْتُ وَزِيرِى الْكَبِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-tarahhama ʿalayhi al-sulṭānu wa-qāla lahu ayyuhā al-ṣāḥibu kāna wazīrī wa-kuntu uḥibbuhu kathīran min muddati khamsata ʿashara sanatan wa-māta wa-khallafa waladan wa-mā aqāma baʿda mawtihi illā shahran wāḥidan wa-laqad tāha wa-lam naṭṭaliʿ lahu ʿalā khabarin ghayra anna ummahu ʿindanā li-annahā bintu wazīrī al-kabīri
sentences.l: So-he-invoked-mercy upon-him, the-sultan, and-said to-him: O the-companion, he-was my-vizier, and-I-was loving-him much from a-period-of fifteen years; and-he-died and-left-behind a-son; and-not he-stayed after his-death except a-month one; and-indeed he-got-lost; and-not we-learned of-him any news, except that his-mother (is) with-us, because-she (is) daughter-of my-vizier the-great.
sentences.i: The sultan prayed God's mercy upon him, and said: "My friend, he was my vizier, and I loved him dearly for fifteen years. He died and left a son, who stayed only a single month after his father's death, and then was lost; and we have had no word of him. Only his mother is with us, for she is the daughter of my chief vizier."
sentences.n: The subject of وَمَا اَقَامَ and وَلَقَدْتَاهَ is the son, not the vizier. وَلَقَدْتَاهَ is run together: وَلَقَدْ تَاهَ, "and indeed he wandered off, was lost". غَيْرَاَنَّ is غير أن, "except that". وَزِيرِى is printed with ى for ي. الصاحب, "friend", is the sultan's courteous address to the visiting vizier.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ مِنَ الْمَلِكِ أَنَّ أُمَّ ابْنِ أَخِيهِ طَيِّبَةٌ فَرِحَ وَقَالَ يَامَلِكُ إِنِّي أُرِيدُأَنْ أَجْتَمِعَ بِهَا فَفِى الْحَالِ أَذِنَ لَهُ وَدَخَلَ إِلَيْهَا فِي دَارِ أَخِيهِ نُورِالدِّينِ فَجَالَ بِبَصَرِهِ فِي نَوَاحِيهَا وَقَبَّلَ أَعْتَابَهَا وَافْتَكَرَ أَخَاهُ نُورَالدِّينِ عَلِي وَكَيْفَ مَاتَ غَرِيبًا فَبَكَى وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru shamsu al-dīni mina al-maliki anna umma ibni akhīhi ṭayyibatun fariḥa wa-qāla yāmaliku innī urīdu an ajtamiʿa bihā fa-fī al-ḥāli adhina lahu wa-dakhala ilayhā fī dāri akhīhi nūri al-dīni fa-jāla bi-baṣarihi fī nawāḥīhā wa-qabbala aʿtābahā wa-iftakara akhāhu nūra al-dīni ʿalī wa-kayfa māta gharīban fa-bakā wa-anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And-when heard the-vizier Shams al-Dīn from the-king that the-mother-of the-son-of his-brother (was) well, he-rejoiced and-said: O-king, indeed-I I-want that I-meet with-her. So-in the-moment he-gave-leave to-him, and-he-entered to-her in the-house-of his-brother Nūr al-Dīn; so-he-passed with-his-sight in its-quarters, and-kissed its-thresholds, and-recalled his-brother Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and-how he-died a-stranger; so-he-wept and-recited, saying:
sentences.i: When the vizier Shams al-Dīn heard from the king that the mother of his nephew was alive and well, he rejoiced, and said, "O king, I wish to meet her." The king gave him leave at once, and he went in to her, in the house of his brother Nūr al-Dīn. He let his eyes pass over its quarters, kissed its thresholds, and called to mind his brother Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, and how he had died far from home; so he wept, and recited:
sentences.n: يَامَلِكُ is يا ملك, run together. طَيِّبَةٌ, "good", here means well, in good health. فَفِى الْحَالِ, "in the moment", is "at once". The vizier is introduced twice by title and name: الْوَزِيرُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ is "the vizier, Shams al-Dīn".

sentences.t:
اَمُرُّ عَلَى الدِّيَارِ دِيَارِ لَيْلَى * اُقَبِّلُ ذَا الْجِدَارِ وَذَا الْجِدَارَا
وَمَا حُبُّ الدِّيَارِ شَغَفْنَ قَلْبِي * وَلَكِنْ حُبُّ مَنْ سَكَنَ الدِّيَارَا
sentences.tr:
amurru ʿalā al-diyāri diyāri laylā * uqabbilu dhā al-jidāri wa-dhā al-jidārā
wa-mā ḥubbu al-diyāri shaghafna qalbī * wa-lakin ḥubbu man sakana al-diyārā
sentences.l:
I-pass over the-abodes, the-abodes-of Laylā; * I-kiss this-one-of the-wall and-this-one-of the-wall.
And-not (is) the-love-of the-abodes (what) ravished my-heart, * but the-love-of him-who dwelt the-abodes.
sentences.i: I pass by the dwellings, the dwellings of Laylā, and kiss this wall and that wall. It is not love of the dwellings that has ravished my heart, but love of him who dwelt in them.
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. اَمُرُّ and اُقَبِّلُ have no printed hamza (read أَمُرُّ, أُقَبِّلُ). شَغَفْنَ is a feminine-plural verb agreeing with الدِّيَارِ, "the dwellings". The verse gives a lover's reason for kissing walls: the walls are not the beloved, but hold the memory of the beloved; here Shams al-Dīn borrows it for his lost brother.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَ مِنَ الْبَابِ إِلَى فَسْحَةٍ عَظِيمَةٍ وَبَابٍ مُقَوْصَرٍ مَعْقُودٍ بِالْحَجَرِ الصَّوَّانِ مُجَزَّعٍ بِأَنْوَاعِ الرُّخَامِ مِنْ سَائِرِ الْأَلْوَانِ فَمَشَى فِي نَوَاخِى الدَّارِ وَنَظَرَهَا وَجَالَ بِطَرْفِهِ فِيهَا فَوَجَدَ اسْمَ أَخِيهِ نُورَالدِّينِ مَكْتُوبًا عَلَيْهَا بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhala mina al-bābi ilā fasḥatin ʿaẓīmatin wa-bābin muqawṣarin maʿqūdin bi-al-ḥajari al-ṣawwāni mujazzaʿin bi-anwāʿi al-rukhāmi min sāʾiri al-alwāni fa-mashā fī nawāḥī al-dāri wa-naẓarahā wa-jāla bi-ṭarfihi fīhā fa-wajada isma akhīhi nūri al-dīni maktūban ʿalayhā bi-māʾi al-dhahabi
sentences.l: Then he-entered from the-door to a-court great, and-a-door muqawṣar, vaulted with-the-stone the-flint, variegated with-kinds-of the-marble of all the-colours; and-he-walked in the-quarters-of the-house and-looked-at-it, and-passed with-his-glance in-it, and-found the-name-of his-brother Nūr al-Dīn written upon-it with-water-of the-gold.
sentences.i: Then he passed in at the door to a great open court, and a vaulted gateway of flint stone, streaked with marble of every kind and colour. He walked through the quarters of the house and looked it over, letting his gaze wander about it, and found the name of his brother Nūr al-Dīn written upon it in liquid gold.
sentences.n: مُقَوْصَرٍ is obscure; it may be a corruption of مَقْصُورٍ, "enclosed", or of مُقَوَّسٍ, "arched"; the translation takes it as part of the vaulted gateway. مُجَزَّعٍ means streaked or inlaid in bands of different colours. نَوَاخِى is a slip for نَوَاحِي, "quarters, parts", and is read nawāḥī. نَظَرَهَا takes a direct object where Classical has نَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا. بِمَاءِ الذَّهَبِ, "with water of gold", is gold ink or gilding.

sentences.t: فَأَنَى إِلَى الِاسْمِ وَقَبَّلَهُ وَبَكَى وَتَذَكَّرَ فُرْقَتَهُ فَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَٰذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: fa-atā ilā al-ismi wa-qabbalahu wa-bakā wa-tadhakkara furqatahu fa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: So-he-came to the-name, and-kissed-it, and-wept, and-remembered his-separation, and-recited, saying, these the-verses:
sentences.i: He went up to the name and kissed it, and wept, remembering how he had been parted from him, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: فَاَنَى is printed with ن where فَأَتَى, "and he came", is meant; it is read atā. يَقُولُ هَٰذِهِ الْاَبْيَاتَ, "saying these verses", puts the verses in the accusative as the thing said.

sentences.t:
اَسْتَخْبِرُ الشَّمْسَ عَنْكُمْ كُلَّمَا طَلَعَتْ * وَاسَالُ الْبَرْقَ عَنْكُمْ كُلَّمَا لَمَعَا
اَبِيتُ وَالشَّوْقُ يَطْوِينِي وَيَنْشُرُنِي * فِي رَاحَتَيْهِ وَلَا اَشْكُوا لَهُ وَجَعَا
اَحْبَابُنَا اِنْ يَكُنْ طَالَ الْمُدَا فَكَذَا * فِرَاقُكُمْ قَدْ قَطَعْنَا بَعْدَكُمْ قِطَعَا
فَلَوْ تَمَنَّوْا عَلَى طَرْفِي بِرُؤْيَتِكُمْ * لَكَانَ اَحْسَنَ اِذْ مَا بَيْنَنَا جَمَعَا
لَا تَحْسِبُوا اِنَّنِي بِالْغَيْرِ مُشْتَغِلُ * اِنَّ :الْفُوْءَادَ لِحُبِّ الْغَيْرِ مَا وَسِعَا
sentences.tr:
astakhbiru al-shamsa ʿankum kullamā ṭalaʿat * wa-asʾalu al-barqa ʿankum kullamā lamaʿā
abītu wa-al-shawqu yaṭwīnī wa-yanshurunī * fī rāḥatayhi wa-lā ashkū lahu wajaʿā
aḥbābunā in yakun ṭāla al-mudā fa-kadhā * firāqukum qad qaṭaʿnā baʿdakum qiṭaʿā
fa-law tamannaw ʿalā ṭarfī bi-ruʾyatikum * la-kāna aḥsana idh mā baynanā jamaʿā
lā taḥsabū innanī bi-al-ghayri mushtaghilu * inna :al-fuʾāda li-ḥubbi al-ghayri mā wasiʿā
sentences.l:
I-ask-for-news the-sun of-you whenever it-rose, * and-I-ask the-lightning of-you whenever it-flashed.
I-spend-the-night while the-longing folds-me and-unfolds-me * in its-two-palms, and-not I-complain to-it of-pain.
Our-beloved-ones, if long has-been the-term, so (too is) * your-parting; we-have-cut after-you pieces.
So-if they-wished upon my-eye the-sight-of-you, * it-would-be fairer, since what (is) between-us it-gathered.
Do-not suppose that-I (am) with-the-other occupied; * indeed the-heart for-the-love-of the-other not it-has-held-room.
sentences.i: I ask the sun for news of you each time it rises, and ask the lightning of you each time it flashes. I pass my nights while longing folds me up and unfolds me in its palm, and I complain to it of no pain. Beloved ones, if the time has been long, so too has your parting; since you left we have cut through whole stretches. If they would grant my eye the sight of you, it would be far better, now that what lies between us has been gathered up. Do not suppose that I am taken up with another: the heart has no room for the love of anyone else.
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. The print leaves hamza unmarked in اَسْتَخْبِرُ, وَاسَالُ, اَبِيتُ, اَشْكُوا (read أَشْكُو, with the rhyme's long vowel), اَحْبَابُنَا, اَحْسَنَ, اِنْ, اِذْ, اِنَّ and اِنَّنِي. الْمُدَا stands for الْمُدَّةِ, "the term". مُشْتَغِلُ has no tanwīn, and a stray colon stands before الْفُوْءَادَ; both are kept as printed. قِطَعًا, "pieces", is read as stretches of road or night. The hemistich فَلَوْ تَمَنَّوْا … اِذْ مَا بَيْنَنَا جَمَعَا is obscure, and the translation gives only its likeliest sense.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ صَارَ يَمْشِي إِلَى أَنْ جَاءَ إِلَى قَاعَةِ زَوْجَةِ أَخِيهِ أُمِّ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ الْمِصْرِيِّ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ṣāra yamshī ilā an jāʾa ilā qāʿati zawjati akhīhi ummi badri al-dīni ḥasanin al-miṣriyyi
sentences.l: Then indeed-he began, he-walks, until he-came to the-hall-of the-wife-of his-brother, the-mother-of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan the-Egyptian,
sentences.i: Then he walked on until he came to the hall of his brother's wife, the mother of Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan the Egyptian.

sentences.t: وَكَانَتْ فِي مُدَّةِ غَيْبَةِ وَلَدِهَا لَزِمَتِ الْبُكَاءَ وَالنَّحِيبَ بِا للَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ فَلَمَّا طَالَتْ عَلَيْهَا السِّنِينَ عَمِلَتْ لِوَلَدِهَا قَبْرًا مِنَ الرُّخَامِ فِي وَسَطِ الْقَاعَةِ وَصَارَتْ تَبْكِي عَلَيْهِ لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا لَاتَنَامُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ الْقَبْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-kānat fī muddati ghaybati waladihā lazimati al-bukāʾa wa-al-naḥība bi-al-layli wa-al-nahāri fa-lammā ṭālat ʿalayhā al-sinīna ʿamilat li-waladihā qabran mina al-rukhāmi fī wasaṭi al-qāʿati wa-ṣārat tabkī ʿalayhi laylan wa-nahāran lā-tanāmu illā ʿinda dhālika al-qabri
sentences.l: And-she-was, in the-period-of the-absence-of her-son, she-clung-to the-weeping and-the-wailing by-the-night and-the-day. And-when long-grew upon-her the-years, she-made for-her-son a-tomb of the-marble in the-middle-of the-hall, and-began weeping over-him night and-day, not-sleeping except at that the-tomb.
sentences.i: All the time her son was away she had given herself up to weeping and wailing, night and day. And when the years grew long upon her she had a tomb of marble made for her son in the middle of the hall, and went on weeping over it night and day, sleeping nowhere but beside that tomb.
sentences.n: وَكَانَتْ … لَزِمَتِ, "she was ... she clung", is the ordinary "she had clung". السِّنِينَ is in the oblique form where the nominative السِّنُونَ would be expected as subject of طَالَتْ, a common Middle Arabic levelling. بِا للَّيْلِ is بالليل with a space printed inside it.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَ الْوَزِيرُ إِلَى مَسْكَنِهَا سَمِعَ حِسَّهَا فَوَقَفَ خَلْفَ الْبَابِ فَسَمِعَهَا تُنْشِدُ عَلَى الْقَبْرِ وَتَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣala al-wazīru ilā maskanihā samiʿa ḥissahā fa-waqafa khalfa al-bābi fa-samiʿahā tunshidu ʿalā al-qabri wa-taqūlu
sentences.l: And-when arrived the-vizier at her-dwelling, he-heard her-sound, and-stood behind the-door, and-heard-her reciting over the-tomb and-saying:
sentences.i: When the vizier reached her dwelling he heard her voice, and stood behind the door; and he heard her reciting beside the tomb, saying:

sentences.t:
بِاللّٰهِ يَا قَبْرُ هَلْ زَالَتْ مَحَاسِنُهُ * وَهَلْ تَغَيَّرَ ذَاكَ الْمَنْظَرُ النَّضِرُ
يَاقَبْرُ مَا اَنْتَ لَارَوْضٌ وَلَا فَلَكٌ * فَكَيْفَ يَجْمَعُ فِيكَ الْغُصْنُ وَالْقَمَرُ
sentences.tr:
bi-Allāhi yā qabru hal zālat maḥāsinuhu * wa-hal taghayyara dhāka al-manẓaru al-naḍiru
yāqabru mā anta lā rawḍun wa-lā falakun * fa-kayfa yajmaʿu fīka al-ghuṣnu wa-al-qamaru
sentences.l:
By-God, O tomb, have-gone his-beauties, * and-has-changed that the-sight the-radiant?
O-tomb, not you (are) a-garden nor a-sphere; * so-how does-it-gather in-you the-branch and-the-moon?
sentences.i: By God, O tomb, have his fair features passed away, and has that radiant face changed? O tomb, you are neither a garden nor a heaven: how then can the bough and the moon be joined within you?
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. اَنْتَ has no printed hamza (read أَنْتَ). يَجْمَعُ is pointed as an active, "does gather", where the sense wants a passive (يُجْمَعُ, "are gathered"); the print is kept. The "branch" and the "moon" are the young man's slender form and shining face. فَلَك is the heavenly sphere.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هِيَ كَذَٰلِكَ وَإِذَا بِالْوَزِيرِ شَمْسِ الدِّينِ قَدْ دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا وَسَلَّمَ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hiya ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-al-wazīri shamsi al-dīni qad dakhala ʿalayhā wa-sallama
sentences.l: And-while she (was) thus, and-behold, with-the-vizier Shams al-Dīn: he-had entered upon-her and-greeted.
sentences.i: While she was so, behold, the vizier Shams al-Dīn had come in to her and given greeting.
sentences.n: After وَاِ_ذَا of surprise, بِالْوَزِيرِ marks what suddenly appears: "and behold, the vizier".

sentences.t: وَأَعْلَمَهَا أَنَّهُ أَخُو زَوْجِهَا ثُمَّ أَخْبَرَهَا بِمَا جَرَٰي وَكَشَفَ لَهَا عَنِ الْقِصَّةِ وَأَنَّ ابْنَهَا بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ بَاتَ عِنْدَ ابْنَتِهِ لَيْلَةً كَامِلَةً مِنْ مُدَّةِ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ وَفُقِدَ عِنْدَ الصَّبَاحِ وَأَنَّ ابْنَتِي حَمَلَتْ مِنْ وَلَدِكِ وَوَلَدَتْ وَلَدًا وَهُوَ مَعِي وَأَنَّهُ وَلَدُكِ وَوَلَدُ وَلَدِكِ مِنِ ابْنَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-aʿlamahā annahu akhū zawjihā thumma akhbarahā bi-mā jarā wa-kashafa lahā ʿani al-qiṣṣati wa-anna ibnahā badra al-dīni ḥasana bāta ʿinda ibnatihi laylatan kāmilatan min muddati ʿashri sinīna wa-fuqida ʿinda al-ṣabāḥi wa-anna ibnatī ḥamalat min waladiki wa-waladat waladan wa-huwa maʿī wa-annahu waladuki wa-waladu waladiki mini ibnatī
sentences.l: And-he-informed-her that-he (is) brother-of her-husband; then he-told-her of-what had-happened, and-uncovered to-her concerning the-story; and-that her-son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan spent-the-night with his-daughter a-full night, from a-period-of ten years, and-was-lost at the-morning; and-that my-daughter conceived from your-son, and-bore a-son, and-he (is) with-me; and-that-he (is) your-child and-the-child-of your-child from my-daughter.
sentences.i: He made known to her that he was her husband's brother, then told her what had happened and laid the whole story open to her: that her son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan had passed one whole night with his daughter, ten years before, and had been lost at dawn; that his daughter had conceived by her son and borne a boy; and that the boy was with him, her own son's son, born of his daughter.
sentences.n: The account slips from third person (ابْنَتِهِ, "his daughter") to first (ابْنَتِي, "my daughter"), as reported speech often does. أَخُو is the nominative construct form of "brother", printed with a final waw. مِنْ مُدَّةِ عَشْرِ سِنِينَ, "from a period of ten years", means ten years ago. وَلَدِكِ is pointed with the feminine kasra, since she is addressed.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ خَبَرَ وَلَدِهَا وَأَنَّهُ حَيٌّ وَرَأَتْ سِلْفَهَا فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ قَامَتْ لَهُ وَوَقَعَتْ عَلَى أَقْدَامِهِ وَقَبَّلَتْهَا وَأَنْشَدَتْ تَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat khabara waladihā wa-annahu ḥayyun wa-raʾat silfahā fa-ʿinda dhālika qāmat lahu wa-waqaʿat ʿalā aqdāmihi wa-qabbalathā wa-anshadat taqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: And-when she-heard news-of her-son and-that-he (is) alive, and-saw her-brother-in-law, then at that she-rose to-him, and-fell upon his-feet and-kissed-them, and-recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: When she heard the news of her son, that he was alive, and saw her husband's brother, she rose before him, fell at his feet and kissed them, and recited these verses:
sentences.n: فَعِنْدَ ذَٰلِكَ, "then, at that", opens the main clause after the long فَلَمَّا clause (the فَـ answers the "when"). سِلْفَهَا is a husband's brother, here Shams al-Dīn.

sentences.t:
لِلّٰهِ دَرُّ مُبَشِّرِي بِقُدُومِهِمْ * فَلَقَدْ اَتَى يَا طَائِبِ الْمَسْمُوعِ
لَوْ كَانَ يَقْنَعُ بِالْخَلِيعِ وَهَبْتُهُ * قَلْبًا تَقَطَّعَ سَاعَةَ التَّوْدِيعِ
sentences.tr:
li-Allāhi darru mubashshirī bi-qudūmihim * fa-laqad atā yā ṭāʾibi al-masmūʿi
law kāna yaqnaʿu bi-al-khalīʿi wahabtuhu * qalban taqaṭṭaʿa sāʿata al-tawdīʿi
sentences.l:
To-God (be) the-abundance-of the-bringer-of-glad-tidings-to-me of-their-coming! * For-indeed he-has-come, O ṭāʾib-of the-heard!
If he-were content with-the-cast-off, I-would-give-him * a-heart that-was-cut-to-pieces the-hour-of the-farewell.
sentences.i: How excellent is the one who brings me glad news of their coming! For he has come: O sweetness of what is heard! If he would be content with a cast-off wretch, I would give him a heart that was torn to pieces at the hour of farewell.
sentences.n: Pointing as printed. لِلّٰهِ دَرُّ ... is a stock phrase of admiration, "to God belongs the excellence of ...". يَا طَائِبِ الْمَسْمُوعِ is obscure; طَائِب, "repenting", makes poor sense and is probably for طَيِّب or طِيب, "O goodness of the news heard", and the translation takes it so. الْخَلِيع, "cast-off, disowned", is probably the speaker herself, forsaken and worn out by grief. اَتَى has no printed hamza.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْوَزِيرَ أَرْسَلَ خَلْفَ عَجِيبٍ يُحْضِرُهُ فَلَمَّا حَضَرَ قَامَتْ جَدَّتُهُ وَاعْتَنَقَتْهُ وَبَكَتْ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-wazīra arsala khalfa ʿajībin yuḥḍiruhu fa-lammā ḥaḍara qāmat jaddatuhu wa-iʿtanaqathu wa-bakat
sentences.l: Then indeed the-vizier sent after ʿAjīb, to-bring-him; and-when he-came, rose his-grandmother and-embraced-him and-wept.
sentences.i: Then the vizier sent for ʿAjīb to be brought to him; and when the boy came, his grandmother rose, embraced him, and wept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا شَمْسُالدِّينِ مَا هَذَا وَقْتُ بُكَاءٍ هَذَا وَقْتُ تَجْهِيزِكِ لِلسَّفَرِ مَعَنَا إِلَى دِيَارِ مِصْرَ عَسَىاللَّهُ يَجْمَعُ شَمْلَنَا وَشَمْلَكِ بِوَالِدِكِ ابْنِ أَخِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā shamsu al-dīni mā hādhā waqtu bukāʾin hādhā waqtu tajhīziki li-al-safari maʿanā ilā diyāri miṣra ʿasā Allāhu yajmaʿu shamlanā wa-shamlaki bi-wālidiki ibni akhī
sentences.l: And-he-said to-her, Shams al-Dīn: Not this a-time of-weeping; this a-time of-your-preparing for-the-journey with-us to the-abodes of-Egypt. Perhaps-God he-will-gather our-union and-your-union with-your-begetter, son of-my-brother.
sentences.i: And Shams al-Dīn said to her, "This is no time for weeping; it is time for you to make ready to journey with us to the land of Egypt. Perhaps God will unite us and you with your son, my brother's son."
sentences.n: عسىالله يجمع is run together in the print; the indicative يَجْمَعُ after عَسَى is a Middle Arabic looseness (Classical has the subjunctive). بوالدك is printed with والد, "father, parent", where the sense wants وَلَدِكِ, "your son": the speaker means Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, the old woman's son and his own brother's son. It may be a slip in the print; the pointing follows the letters as printed.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qālat samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And-she-said: Hearing and-obedience.
sentences.i: And she said, with hearing and obedience.
sentences.n: سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً, "with hearing and obedience", is the standard formula of assent: the speaker offers hearing and obedience in place of a verb, and it recurs throughout the Nights.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَامَتْ مِنْ وَقْتِهَا وَجَمَعَتْ مَصَالِحَهَا وَذَخَائِرَهَا وَجَوَارِهَا وَفِىالْحَالِ تَجَهَّزَتْ وَطَلَعَ الْوَزِيرُ شَمْسُالدِّينِ إِلَى سُلْطَانِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَوَدَّعَهُ فَبَعَثَ مَعَهُ هَدَايَا وَتُحَفْ إِلَى سُلْطَانِ مِصْرَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāmat min waqtihā wa-jamaʿat maṣāliḥahā wa-dhakhāʾirahā wa-jawārihā wa-fī al-ḥāli tajahhazat wa-ṭalaʿa al-wazīru shamsu al-dīni ilā sulṭāni al-baṣrati wa-waddaʿahu fa-baʿatha maʿahu hadāyā wa-tuḥaf ilā sulṭāni miṣra
sentences.l: Then she-rose from her-time and-gathered her-belongings and-her-treasures and-her-slave-girls, and-in-the-moment she-made-ready; and-went-up the-vizier Shams al-Dīn to sultan-of Basra and-took-leave-of-him, and-he-sent with-him gifts and-rarities to sultan-of Egypt.
sentences.i: Then she rose at once, gathered her belongings, her treasures and her slave-girls, and in a moment she was ready. And the vizier Shams al-Dīn went to the sultan of Basra and took leave of him, and the sultan sent with him gifts and rarities for the sultan of Egypt.
sentences.n: جوارها is printed without the yā of جَوَارِيهَا, "her slave-girls"; it is read jawārīhā. The sultan of Basra is the one who sends the gifts.

sentences.t: وَسَافَرَ مِنْ وَقْتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ فَنَزَلَ فِىالْقَانُونِ وَضَرَبَ الْخِيَامَ وَقَالَ لِمَنْ مَعَهُ نُقِيمُ بِهَا جُمْعَةً إِلَى أَنْ نَشْتَرِيَ لِلسُّلْطَانِ هَدَايَا وَتُحَفْ
sentences.tr: wa-sāfara min waqtihi ilā an waṣala ilā madīnati dimashqa fa-nazala fī al-qānūni wa-ḍaraba al-khiyāma wa-qāla li-man maʿahu nuqīmu bihā jumʿatan ilā an nashtariya li-al-sulṭāni hadāyā wa-tuḥaf
sentences.l: And-he-travelled from his-time until he-arrived to city-of Damascus, and-alighted at-the-Qānūn and-pitched the-tents, and-said to-those-who with-him: We-shall-stay in-it a-week until we-buy for-the-sultan gifts and-rarities.
sentences.i: And he set out at once and journeyed until he reached the city of Damascus, where he halted at the Qānūn and pitched the tents. And he said to those with him, "We shall stay here a week, while we buy gifts and rarities for the sultan."
sentences.n: القانون here seems to be a place-name, perhaps a stopping-ground outside Damascus; I take it so, with some doubt. جمعة is "a week" (it is also the word for Friday).

sentences.t: وَقَدْ خَرَجَ عَجِيبٌ فَقَالَ لِلطَّوَاشِي يَا لَايِقُ إِنِّي اشْتَقْتُ إِلَى الْفُرْجَةِ فَقُمْ بِنَا نَنْزِلْ إِلَىالسُّوقِ وَنَعْبُرْ دِمَشْقَ وَنَنْظُرْ مَا جَرَى لِذَلِكَ الطَّبَّاخِ الَّذِي كُنَّا قَدْ أَكَلْنَا طَعَامَهُ وَشَجَيْنَا رَأْسَهُ وَهُوَ قَدْ كَانَ أَحْسَنَ إِلَيْنَا وَنَحْنُ أَسَأْنَاهُ
sentences.tr: wa-qad kharaja ʿajībun fa-qāla li-al-ṭawāshī yā lāyiqu innī ishtaqtu ilā al-furjati fa-qum binā nanzil ilā al-sūqi wa-naʿbur dimashqa wa-nanẓur mā jarā li-dhālika al-ṭabbākhi alladhī kunnā qad akalnā ṭaʿāmahu wa-shajaynā raʾsahu wa-huwa qad kāna aḥsana ilaynā wa-naḥnu asaʾnāhu
sentences.l: And-already had-gone-out ʿAjīb, and-he-said to-the-eunuch: O Lāʾiq, indeed-I I-have-longed for-the-outing, so-rise with-us, let-us-go-down to-the-market and-pass-through Damascus and-look what happened to-that the-cook who we-had we-eaten his-food and-we-wounded his-head, and-he was-kind to-us and-we wronged-him.
sentences.i: Now ʿAjīb had gone out, and he said to the eunuch, "Lāʾiq, I long for an outing. Come, let us go down to the market, stroll through Damascus, and see what became of that cook whose food we ate and whose head we split; he had been kind to us, and we had wronged him."
sentences.n: The eunuch's name is printed لايق, read Lāʾiq ("fitting"). وَشَجَيْنَا رَأْسَهُ, "we wounded his head", recalls the stone ʿAjīb threw at the cook in an earlier scene.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الطَّوَاشِي سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṭawāshī samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: And-said the-eunuch: Hearing and-obedience.
sentences.i: And the eunuch said, with hearing and obedience.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَجِيبًا خَرَجَ مِنَ الْخِيَامِ هُوَ وَالطَّوَاشِي وَحَرَّكَتْهُ الْقَرَابَةُ لِوَالِدِهِ وَفِىالْحَالِ دَخَلُوا إِلَىالْمَدِينَةِ وَمَا زَالُوا سَائِرِينَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلُوا إِلَى دُكَّانِ الطَّبَّاخِ فَوَجَدَهُ وَاقِفًا فِىالدُّكَّانِ وَكَانَ الْوَقْتُ قَرِيبَ الْعَصْرِ وَقَدْ وَافَقَ الْأَمْرُ أَنَّهُ طَبَخَ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ
sentences.tr: thumma inna ʿajīban kharaja mina al-khiyāmi huwa wa-al-ṭawāshī wa-ḥarrakathu al-qarābatu li-wālidihi wa-fī al-ḥāli dakhalū ilā al-madīnati wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna ilā an waṣalū ilā dukkāni al-ṭabbākhi fa-wajadahu wāqifan fī al-dukkāni wa-kāna al-waqtu qarība al-ʿaṣri wa-qad wāfaqa al-amru annahu ṭabakha ḥabba rummānin
sentences.l: Then indeed ʿAjīb went-out from the-tents, he and-the-eunuch, and-stirred-him the-kinship for-his-father; and-at-the-moment they-entered to-the-city, and-not they-ceased going until they-arrived to shop-of the-cook, and-he-found-him standing in-the-shop; and-was the-time near the-ʿaṣr; and-it-so-fell-out the-matter that-he cooked seeds-of pomegranate.
sentences.i: Then ʿAjīb went out from the tents with the eunuch, the tie of blood stirring him toward his father; and at once they entered the city and went on walking until they came to the cook's shop, and found him standing in it. It was near the hour of the afternoon prayer, and it so happened that he had cooked pomegranate seeds.
sentences.n: The cook is Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, ʿAjīb's father, whom the boy does not know; the narrator says the blood-tie moved him.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا قَرُبَا مِنْهُ وَنَظَرَ عَجِيبٌ إِلَيْهِ حَنَّ لَهُ وَنَظَرَ إِلَى أَثَرِ الضَّرْبَةِ بِالْحَجَرِ فِي جَبِينِهِ فَقَالَ لَهُ السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ يَا هَذَا اعْلَمْ أَنَّ خَاطِرِي عِنْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā qarubā minhu wa-naẓara ʿajībun ilayhi ḥanna lahu wa-naẓara ilā athari al-ḍarbati bi-al-ḥajari fī jabīnihi fa-qāla lahu al-salāmu ʿalayka yā hādhā iʿlam anna khāṭirī ʿindaka
sentences.l: And-when the-two-drew-near to-him, and-looked ʿAjīb at-him, he-yearned for-him, and-looked at mark-of the-blow with-the-stone in his-brow; and-he-said to-him: Peace upon-you, O this-one; know that my-heart (is) with-you.
sentences.i: When the two drew near him, and ʿAjīb looked at him, he felt a yearning toward him, and saw the mark of the stone's blow on his brow. And he said to him, "Peace be upon you, friend; know that my heart is with you."

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ بَدْرُالدِّينِ تَقَلْقَلَتْ أَحْشَاؤُهُ وَخَفَقَ فُؤَادُهُ وَأَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ وَ أَرَادَأَنْ يُدِيرَ لِسَانَهُ فِي فَمِهِ فَمَا قَدَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓara ilayhi badru al-dīni taqalqalat aḥshāʾuhu wa-khafaqa fuʾāduhu wa-aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi ilā al-arḍi wa arāda an yudīra lisānahu fī famihi fa-mā qadara
sentences.l: And-when he-looked at-him, Badr al-Dīn, shook his-entrails and-throbbed his-heart, and-he-bowed with-his-head to the-ground, and and-wanted-to he-turn his-tongue in his-mouth, but-not he-could.
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn looked at him, his entrails quaked and his heart pounded; he bowed his head to the ground and tried to move his tongue in his mouth, but could not.
sentences.n: أرادان is أَرَادَ أَنْ run together, "he wanted to". The lone و at the end of the previous printed line belongs to it ("and he wanted").

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ رَفَعَ رَأْسَهُ إِلَى وَلَدِهِ خَاضِعًا مُتَذَلِّلًا وَأَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu rafaʿa raʾsahu ilā waladihi khāḍiʿan mutadhallilan wa-anshada yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāba
sentences.l: Then indeed-he raised his-head to his-son, submissive, abasing-himself, and-recited, saying, these the-verses.
sentences.i: Then he raised his head to his son, humble and abject, and recited these verses.
sentences.n: الابياب is a misprint for الأبيات, "the verses"; the pointing follows the letters as printed.

sentences.t:
تَمَنَّيْتُ مَنْ اَهْوَى فَلَمَّا رَاَيْتُهُ * ذَهَلْتُ فَلَمْ اَمْلِكْ لِسَانًا وَلَا طَرْفَا
وَاَطْرَقْتُ اِجْلَالاً لَهُ وَمَهَــابَةً * وَحَاوَلْتُ اَنْ اُخْفِىَ الَّذِي بِي فَلَمْ يَخْفَى
وَقَدْ كَانَ عِنْدِي لِلْعِتَابِ دَفَاتِرُ * فَلَمَّا الْتَقَيْنَا مَا نَطَقْتُ وَلَا حَرْفاً
sentences.tr:
tamannaytu man ahwā fa-lammā raaytuhu * dhahaltu fa-lam amlik lisānan wa-lā ṭarfā
wa-aṭraqtu ijlālan lahu wa-mahābatan * wa-ḥāwaltu an ukhfiya alladhī bī fa-lam yakhfā
wa-qad kāna ʿindī li-al-ʿitābi dafātiru * fa-lammā iltaqaynā mā naṭaqtu wa-lā ḥarfan
sentences.i: I longed for the one I love, and when I saw him I was stunned, and had mastery of neither tongue nor glance. I bowed my head in reverence for him and in awe, and tried to hide what is within me, but it would not stay hidden. I had ledgers full of reproach; yet when we met I could not utter so much as a letter.
sentences.n: يَخْفَى stands after لَمْ, where the jussive يَخْفَ is expected; the printed pointing is kept. دَفَاتِرُ, "registers", is the poet's figure for the grievances he had stored up to charge his beloved with.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُمْ اجْبُرُوا قَلْبِي وَكُلُوا مِنْ طَعَــامِي فَوَاللَّهِ مَا نَظَرْتُ إِلَيْكَ إِلَّا خَفَقَ قَلْبِي وَمَا كُنْتُ تَبِعْتُكَ إِلَّاوَأَنَا فِي غَيْرِ عَقْلِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahum ujburū qalbī wa-kulū min ṭaʿāmī fa-wa-Allāhi mā naẓartu ilayka illā khafaqa qalbī wa-mā kuntu tabiʿtuka illā wa-anā fī ghayri ʿaqlī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-them: Console my-heart and-eat from my-food; for-by-God, not I-looked at-you except throbbed my-heart, and-not I-was I-followed-you except-while-I in other-than my-mind.
sentences.i: Then he said to them, "Console my heart, and eat of my food; for by God, I never looked at you but my heart throbbed, and I followed you only because I was beside myself."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ وَاللَّهِ أَنْتَ مُحِبٌّ لَنَا وَنَحْنُ أَكَلْنَا عِنْدَكَ لُقْمَةً لَزِمَتْنَا عَقِبَهَا وَأَرَدْتَ تَهْتِكُنَا وَنَحْنُ لَانَا كُلُ لَكَ أَكْلًا إِلَّا بِشَرْطٍ أَنْ تَحْلِفَ أَنَّكَ لَا تَخْرُجُ وَرَاءَنَا وَلَا تَتْبَعُنَا وَإِلَّا لَانَعُودُ إِلَيْكَ مِنْ وَقْتِنَا هَذَا فَنَحْنُ مُقِيمُونَ جُمْعَةً حَتَّى يَأْخُذَ جَدِّي هَذَا يَا لِلْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ʿajībun wa-Allāhi anta muḥibbun lanā wa-naḥnu akalnā ʿindaka luqmatan lazimatnā ʿaqibahā wa-aradta tahtikunā wa-naḥnu lā nākulu laka aklan illā bi-sharṭin an taḥlifa annaka lā takhruju warāʾanā wa-lā tatbaʿunā wa-illā lā naʿūdu ilayka min waqtinā hādhā fa-naḥnu muqīmūna jumʿatan ḥattā yaʾkhudha jaddī hādhā yā li-al-maliki
sentences.l: And-said ʿAjīb: By-God, you (are) a-lover of-us; and-we ate at-you a-morsel it-bound-us in-its-wake, and-you-wanted to-disgrace-us; and-we, not we-eat for-you any-eating except on-condition you-swear that-you not you-go-out behind-us and-not you-follow-us; and-otherwise not we-return to-you from our-time this; for-we staying a-week until he-takes my-grandfather this, O for-the-king.
sentences.i: And ʿAjīb said, "By God, you are fond of us. We ate one morsel at your shop and it has bound us in your debt, and now you would shame us. We shall eat nothing of yours unless you swear that you will not come out after us nor follow us; otherwise we shall not come back to you from this hour. We are staying a week, until my grandfather has taken this to the king."
sentences.n: The print splits نَأْكُلُ, "we eat", as لانا كل, dropping the hamza (the same Middle Arabic habit as the bare imperative كُلْ). The last clause, حتى ياخذ جدي هذا يا للملك, is obscure; I read it as "until my grandfather takes this (the gifts) to the king", but the sense is a guess and يا للملك may be a corruption.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ لَكُمْ ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla badru al-dīni lakum dhālika
sentences.l: And-said Badr al-Dīn: To-you that.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn said, "You shall have that."

sentences.t: فَدَخَلَ عَجِيبٌ وَالْخَادِمُ الدُّكَّانَ فَقَدَّمَ لَهُمْ زُبْدِيَّةَ حَبِّ رُمَّانٍ فَقَالَ عَجِيبٌ كُلْ مَعَنَا لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُفَرِّجُ عَنَّا
sentences.tr: fa-dakhala ʿajībun wa-al-khādimu al-dukkāna fa-qaddama lahum zubdiyyata ḥabbi rummānin fa-qāla ʿajībun kul maʿanā laʿalla Allāha yufarriju ʿannā
sentences.l: And-entered ʿAjīb and-the-servant the-shop, and-he-set-before them a-bowl of-seeds-of pomegranate; and-said ʿAjīb: Eat with-us, perhaps God he-will-relieve us.
sentences.i: So ʿAjīb and the servant went into the shop, and he set before them a bowl of pomegranate seeds. And ʿAjīb said, "Eat with us; perhaps God will relieve us."

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ وَأَكَلَ مَعَهُمْ وَهُوَ بَاهِتٌ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَقَدْ تَعَلَّقَ قَلْبُهُ وَجَوَارِحُهُ مَعَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa badru al-dīni wa-akala maʿahum wa-huwa bāhitun fī wajhihi wa-qad taʿallaqa qalbuhu wa-jawāriḥuhu maʿahu
sentences.l: And-rejoiced Badr al-Dīn and-ate with-them, and-he dazed at his-face; and-had-clung his-heart and-his-limbs with-him.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn rejoiced and ate with them, gazing at the boy's face in a daze, his heart and all his limbs bound to him.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ عَجِيبٌ اعْلَمْ أَنِّي مَا قُلْتُ أَنَّكَ عَاشِقٌ ثَقِيلٌ فَحَسْبُكَ تُطِيلُ النَّظَرَ إِلَى وَجْهِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu ʿajībun iʿlam annī mā qultu annaka ʿāshiqun thaqīlun fa-ḥasbuka tuṭīlu al-naẓara ilā wajhī
sentences.l: And-said to-him ʿAjīb: Know that-I not I-said that-you (are) a-lover tiresome; so-enough-for-you you-prolong the-gazing at my-face.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb said to him, "Know that I never called you a tiresome lover; but enough now: you are gazing too long at my face."
sentences.n: The boy's remark is playful and a little obscure: he says he has not accused the man of being a wearisome lover, yet the staring has gone on long enough.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ كَلَامَ وَلَدِهِ أَنْشَدَ يَقُ—ولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa badru al-dīni kalāma waladihi anshada yaqūlu
sentences.l: And-when heard Badr al-Dīn the-words-of his-son, he-recited, saying:
sentences.i: When Badr al-Dīn heard his son's words, he recited:

sentences.t:
لَكَ فِي الْقُلُوبِ سَرِيرَةٌ لَا تَظْهَرُ * مَطْوِيَّةٌ مَكْنُونَةٌ لَا تُنْشَرُ
يَافَاضِحَ الْقَمَرِ الْمُنِيرِ بِحُسْنِهِ * وَجَمَالِهِ يُحْكَى الصَّبَاحُ الْمُسْفِرُ
فِي نُورِ وَجْهِكَ مَارِبٌ لَا تَنْقَضِي * وَمَعَاهِدٌ اَبَدًا تَزِيدُ وَتَكْثُرُ
اَذُوبُ مِنْ حَرَقٍ وَوَجْهُكَ جَنَّتِي * وَاَمُوتُ مِنْ ظَمَأٍ وَرِيقُكَ كَوْثَرُ
sentences.tr:
laka fī al-qulūbi sarīratun lā taẓharu * maṭwiyyatun maknūnatun lā tunsharu
yāfāḍiḥa al-qamari al-munīri bi-ḥusnihi * wa-jamālihi yuḥkā al-ṣabāḥu al-musfiru
fī nūri wajhika māribun lā tanqaḍī * wa-maʿāhidun abadan tazīdu wa-taktharu
adhūbu min ḥaraqin wa-wajhuka jannatī * wa-amūtu min ẓamaʾin wa-rīquka kawtharu
sentences.i: You hold in all hearts a secret that never shows, folded away, hidden, never unrolled. O you who shame the shining moon with your beauty, whose loveliness the radiant dawn is likened to: in the light of your face are desires that never end, and haunts that ever grow and multiply. I melt with burning, though your face is my paradise; I die of thirst, though your lips' moisture is Kawthar.
sentences.n: The poet speaks to the beloved but slips into the third person (بحسنه, "with his beauty"), as Arabic verse often does. مَارِب is printed for مَآرِب, "desires, needs". الْكَوْثَر is the river of Paradise, so the last line sets the lover's thirst beside the paradise he cannot reach.

sentences.t: فَصَارَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ يُلَقِّمُ عَجِيبًا سَاعَةً وَيُلَقِّمُ الطَّوَاشِي سَاعَةً فَأَكَلُوا حَتَّى اكْتَفَوْاوَ قَامُوا
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāra badru al-dīni yulaqqimu ʿajīban sāʿatan wa-yulaqqimu al-ṭawāshī sāʿatan fa-akalū ḥattā iktafaw wa-qāmū
sentences.l: And-began Badr al-Dīn he-feeds-morsels ʿAjīb a-while and-feeds-morsels the-eunuch a-while; and-they-ate until they-had-enough and rose.
sentences.i: Badr al-Dīn went on feeding ʿAjīb morsel by morsel for a while, and then the eunuch, and they ate until they had enough, and rose.
sentences.n: The print writes اكتفواو قاموا, attaching the conjunction wāw to the verb before it (اكتفوا و) instead of the verb after; it is read اكتفوا وقاموا, "they had enough and rose".

sentences.t: فَقَامَ حَسَنٌ الْبَصْرِيُّ وَكَبَّ عَلَى أَيْدِيهِمَا الْمَاءَ وَحَلَّ فُوطَةَ حَرِيرٍ مِنْ وَسَطِهِ مَسَحَ أَيْدِيَهُمْ فِيهَا وَرَشَّ عَلَيْهَا الْمَاوَرْدَ مِنْ قُمْقُمٍ كَانَ عِنْدَهُ وَخَرَجَ مِنَ الدُّكَّانِ وَعَادَ بِقُلَّةِ شَرْبَاتٍ مَمْزُوجَةٍ بِالْمَاوَرْدِ الْمُمَسَّكِ وَقَدَّمَهَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَقَالَ أَتِمُّوا إِحْسَانَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāma ḥasanun al-baṣriyyu wa-kabba ʿalā aydīhimā al-māʾa wa-ḥalla fūṭata ḥarīrin min wasaṭihi masaḥa aydiyahum fīhā wa-rashsha ʿalayhā al-māwarda min qumqumin kāna ʿindahu wa-kharaja mina al-dukkāni wa-ʿāda bi-qullati sharbātin mamzūjatin bi-al-māwardi al-mumassaki wa-qaddamahā bayna aydīhim wa-qāla atimmū iḥsānakum
sentences.l: And-rose Ḥasan the-Basran and-poured over their-two-hands the-water, and-untied a-towel-of silk from his-waist, wiped their-hands with-it, and-sprinkled on-them the-rosewater from a-flask which with-him; and-went-out from the-shop and-came-back with-a-jug-of sherbets mixed with-the-rosewater the-musked, and-set-it between their-hands and-said: Complete your-kindness.
sentences.i: Then Ḥasan of Basra got up and poured water over their hands, and untied a silk towel from his waist and wiped their hands with it, and sprinkled them with rosewater from a flask he had by him. He went out of the shop and came back with a jug of sherbets mixed with musked rosewater, and set it before them, and said, "Complete your kindness."
sentences.n: حسن البصري is Badr al-Dīn himself, the name by which the narrator now calls him. اتموا احسانكم, "complete your kindness", asks them to finish by drinking.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَ عَجِيبٌ وَشَرِبَ وَ نَاوَلَ الْخَادِمَ وَتَنَاوَلُوا حَتَّى امْتَلَأَتْ بُطُونُهُمْ وَشَبِعُوا بِخِلَافِ عَادَتِهِمْ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadha ʿajībun wa-shariba wa nāwala al-khādima wa-tanāwalū ḥattā imtalaʾat buṭūnuhum wa-shabiʿū bi-khilāfi ʿādatihim
sentences.l: And-took ʿAjīb and-drank, and handed the-servant, and-they-partook until were-filled their-bellies and-they-were-sated, contrary-to their-habit.
sentences.i: ʿAjīb took it and drank, and passed it to the servant, and they drank in turn until their bellies were full and they were sated, quite against their habit.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ انْصَرَفُوا وَأَسْرَعُوا فِي مَشْيِهِمْ حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى خِيَامِهِمْ وَدَخَلَ عَجِيبٌ عَلَى جَدَّتِهِ أُمِّ وَالِدِهِ بَدْرِالدِّينِ حَسَنٍ فَقَبَّلَتْهُ وَافْتَكَرَتْ وَلَدَهَا بَدْرَالدِّينِ حَسَنَ فَتَنَهَّدَتْ وَبَكَتْ ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا قَالَتْ شِـــــــعْـــــــرٌ
sentences.tr: thumma inṣarafū wa-asraʿū fī mashyihim ḥattā waṣalū ilā khiyāmihim wa-dakhala ʿajībun ʿalā jaddatihi ummi wālidihi badri al-dīni ḥasanin fa-qabbalathu wa-iftakarat waladahā badra al-dīni ḥasana fa-tanahhadat wa-bakat thumma innahā qālat shiʿrun
sentences.l: Then they-departed and-hurried in their-walking until they-arrived to their-tents; and-entered ʿAjīb upon his-grandmother, mother-of his-father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan; and-she-kissed-him and-remembered her-son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan and-sighed and-wept; then indeed-she said: Poetry.
sentences.i: Then they left, and hurried on their way until they came to their tents, and ʿAjīb went in to his grandmother, the mother of his father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan. She kissed him, and remembering her son Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan, she sighed and wept, and then she said in verse:
sentences.n: شعر, "poetry", is printed with its letters stretched out and stands for "she spoke these verses".

sentences.t:
قَدْ كُنتُ اَرْجُو بِاَنَّ الشَّمْلَ يَجْتَمِعُ * مَا كَانَ لِي فِي حَيوتِي بَعْدَ كُمْ طَمَعُ
اَقْسَمْتُ مَافِي فُؤَادِي غَيْرَ حُبِّكُمُ * وَاللّٰهُ رَبِّي عَلَى الْاَسْرَارِ مُطَّلِعُ
sentences.tr:
qad kuntu arjū bi-anna al-shamla yajtamiʿu * mā kāna lī fī ḥayawtī baʿda kum ṭamaʿu
aqsamtu mā fī fuʾādī ghayra ḥubbikumu * wa-Allāhu rabbī ʿalā al-asrāri muṭṭaliʿu
sentences.l:
I-had hoped that the-union would-come-together; * not was to-me in my-life after you any-desire;
I-swore: not in my-heart other-than your-love, * and-God my-Lord (is) aware of the-secrets.
sentences.i: I had hoped that we should be gathered together again; but my life holds no desire for me now, after you. I swear there is nothing in my heart but love of you, and God my Lord is aware of every secret.
sentences.n: حَيوتِي keeps the old Qurʾānic-style spelling of حَيَاتِي, "my life", with a wāw for the long ā; it is read ḥayātī. The suffix of كُمْ is printed as a separate word in بَعْدَ كُمْ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَتْ لِعَجِيبٍ يَا وَلَدِي أَيْنَ كُنْتَ قَالَ فِي مَدِينَةِ دِمَشْقَ فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَامَتْ وَقَدَّمَتْ لَهُ زُبْدِيَّةَ طَعَامٍ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ وَكَانَ قَلِيلَ الْحَلَاوَةِ وَقَالَتْ لِلْخَادِمِ اقْعُدْ مَعَ سَيِّدِكَ
sentences.tr: thumma qālat li-ʿajībin yā waladī ayna kunta qāla fī madīnati dimashqa fa-ʿinda dhālika qāmat wa-qaddamat lahu zubdiyyata ṭaʿāmin ḥabba rummānin wa-kāna qalīla al-ḥalāwati wa-qālat li-al-khādimi uqʿud maʿa sayyidika
sentences.l: Then she-said to-ʿAjīb: O my-son, where you-were? He-said: In city-of Damascus. And-thereupon she-rose and-set-before him a-bowl of-food, seeds-of pomegranate, and-it-was scant-of the-sweetness; and-she-said to-the-servant: Sit with your-master.
sentences.i: Then she said to ʿAjīb, "My son, where have you been?" "In the city of Damascus," he said. Thereupon she rose and set before him a bowl of pomegranate seeds, which was short of sweetness, and she said to the servant, "Sit down with your master."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَادِمُ فِي نَفْسِهِ وَاللَّهِ مَالَنَا نَفْسٌ نَاكُلُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khādimu fī nafsihi wa-Allāhi mā lanā nafsun nākulu
sentences.l: And-said the-servant in his-self: By-God, not-for-us an-appetite we-eat.
sentences.i: And the servant said to himself, "By God, we have no appetite to eat."
sentences.n: ناكل is نَأْكُلُ without its hamza, as in the split لانا كل above; the construction is a bare imperfect after "appetite", "appetite (that) we eat".

sentences.t: وَجَلَسَ الْخَادِمُ وَأَمَّا عَجِيبٌ فَلَمَّا جَلَسَ كَانَتْ بَطْنُهُ مَلْآنَةً مِمَّا أَكَلَ وَشَرِبَ فَأَخَذَ لُقْمَةً وَغَمَسَهَا فِي حَبِّ الرُّمَّانِ وَأَكَلَ فَوَجَدَهُ قَلِيلَ الْحَلَاوَهِ لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ شَبْعَانَ فَقَالَ أُفُوهْ أَيْشْ هَذَا الطَّعَامُ الْوَحْشُ
sentences.tr: wa-jalasa al-khādimu wa-ammā ʿajībun fa-lammā jalasa kānat baṭnuhu malʾānatan mimmā akala wa-shariba fa-akhadha luqmatan wa-ghamasahā fī ḥabbi al-rummāni wa-akala fa-wajadahu qalīla al-ḥalāwahi li-annahu kāna shabʿāna fa-qāla ufūh aysh hādhā al-ṭaʿāmu al-waḥshu
sentences.l: And-sat the-servant; and-as-for ʿAjīb, when he-sat, was his-belly full from-what he-ate and-drank; and-he-took a-morsel and-dipped-it in seeds-of the-pomegranate and-ate, and-found-it scant-of the-sweetness, because-he was sated. And-he-said: Ugh! What (is) this the-food the-foul!
sentences.i: The servant sat down. As for ʿAjīb, when he sat, his belly was full of all he had eaten and drunk; he took a morsel, dipped it in the pomegranate seeds, and ate, and found it short of sweetness, being so full-fed. And he said, "Ugh! What is this foul food?"
sentences.n: الحلاوه is printed with ه for ة; the pointing keeps the printed letter, read ḥalāwa. افوه seems to be an interjection of disgust; I read it ufūh, but the form is not certain. ايش and الوحش are colloquial: "what" and "foul".

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ جَدَّتُهُ يَا وَلَدِي تَعِيبُ عَلَى طَبِيخِي وَأَنَا طَبَخْتُهُ وَلَا يُحْسِنُ أَحَدٌ الطَّبْخَ مِثْلِى إِلَّا وَالِدُكَ بَدْرُالدِّينِ حَسَنٌ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat jaddatuhu yā waladī taʿību ʿalā ṭabīkhī wa-anā ṭabakhtuhu wa-lā yuḥsinu aḥadun al-ṭabkha mithlī illā wāliduka badru al-dīni ḥasanun
sentences.l: And-said his-grandmother: O my-son, you-find-fault with my-cooking, and-I I-cooked-it, and-not does-well anyone the-cooking like-me except your-father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan.
sentences.i: His grandmother said, "My son, do you find fault with my cooking, when I cooked it myself, and no one cooks as well as I, except your father Badr al-Dīn Ḥasan?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ عَجِيبٌ وَاللَّهِ يَاسِتِّي إِنَّ طَبِيخَكِ هَذَا وَحْشٌ نَحْنُ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ رَابَنَا فِى الْمَدِينَةِ طَبَّاخًا طَبَخَ حَبَّ رُمَّانٍ رَائِحَتُهُ يَنْفَتِحُ لَهَا الْقَلْبُ وَأَمَّا طَعَامُهُ فَإِنَّهُ يُشْتَهَي أَنْ يُوكَلَ وَأَمَّا طَعَامُكِ عِنْدَهُ فَلَا يُسَاوِي كَثِيرًا وَلَا قَلِيلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat ʿajībun wa-Allāhi yā sittī inna ṭabīkhaki hādhā waḥshun naḥnu fī hādhihi al-sāʿati rābanā fī al-madīnati ṭabbākhan ṭabakha ḥabba rummānin rāʾiḥatuhu yanfatiḥu lahā al-qalbu wa-ammā ṭaʿāmuhu fa-innahu yushtahā an yūkala wa-ammā ṭaʿāmuki ʿindahu fa-lā yusāwī kathīran wa-lā qalīlan
sentences.l: And-she-said ʿAjīb: By-God, O-my-lady, indeed your-cooking this (is) foul. We, in this the-hour, [rābanā] in the-city a-cook who-cooked seeds-of pomegranate, his-scent opens-for-it the-heart; and-as-for his-food, indeed-it is-desired to-be-eaten; and-as-for your-food, with-him, not is-worth much and-not little.
sentences.i: And ʿAjīb said, "By God, my lady, this cooking of yours is foul. Just now we saw in the city a cook who had cooked pomegranate seeds, and the scent of it opens the heart; his food makes one long to eat it, while your food beside his is worth neither much nor little."
sentences.n: The print has فقالت, a feminine verb, with the masculine ʿAjīb as its subject; read فَقَالَ, but the pointing keeps the letters printed. رابنا is very likely a misprint for رأينا, "we saw" (the letters ب and ي are easily confused); pointed as printed, it would mean "it troubled us", which does not fit. يوكل is yuʾkal, "is eaten", with the hamza unwritten.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ جَدَّتُهُ كَلَامَهُ اغْتَاظَتْ غَيْظًا شَدِيدًا وَنَظَرَتْ إِلَى الْخَادِمِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat jaddatuhu kalāmahu ightāẓat ghayẓan shadīdan wa-naẓarat ilā al-khādimi
sentences.l: And-when heard his-grandmother his-words, she-was-enraged a-rage violent, and-looked at the-servant.
sentences.i: When his grandmother heard what he said, she was filled with violent rage, and she looked at the servant.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَ زَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُـــــــبَـــــــاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahra zāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the formula that closes each night: dawn overtakes Shahrazād, and she falls silent from "permitted speech", the tale she is allowed to tell, until the next evening.
